54.	Regulations generally
	(1)	The Governor may make regulations for and in relation to any matter which the Governor thinks necessary or expedient for carrying this Act into effect, including such transitional, incidental and supplementary provisions as may be necessary in relation to the Acts repealed by this Act or any application of the provisions of this Act.
	(2A)	Without limiting subsection (1), the Governor may make regulations to make provision for a register of dangerous dogs.
	(2B)	Despite the Interpretation Act 1984 section 41(1)(b), a regulation prescribing a breed of dog to be a restricted breed for the purposes of the definition of dangerous dog (restricted breed) in section 3(1) comes into operation on the 7th day after publication in the Gazette or if a later day is specified or provided for in the regulation, on that day.
	(2C)	Without limiting subsection (1), regulations may —
	(a)	require or permit any notice, information or document required or authorised to be given under this Act to be given in a certain way or ways, including —
	(i)	by using the centralised registration system; or
	(ii)	by any other means by which the notice, information or document can be accessed electronically;
		and
	(b)	make provision for or in relation to the time at which the notice, information or document is taken to have been given.
	(2)	Where and to the extent that there is inconsistency between regulations made under this Act and any local law in force in any district made or purporting to have been made under or pursuant to this Act, the Acts repealed by this Act, the Local Government Act 1995, or any other Act the provisions of the regulations prevail.
	(3)	The provisions of section 50(1), (2) and (3) have effect in relation to regulations mentioned in this section in the same way that they apply to a regulation made under section 48.
	[Section 54 amended: No. 14 of 1996 s. 4; No. 18 of 2013 s. 58; No. 29 of 2021 s. 41.]
Division 2 — Local government approvals
	[Heading inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]
Subdivision 1 — Applications for approval
	[Heading inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54A.	Applications
	(1)	An application for the grant of an approval to breed, or for the grant or renewal of a pet shop approval, must —
	(a)	be made in a manner and form approved by the CEO; and
	(b)	contain the information prescribed; and
	(c)	be accompanied by the fee, if any, prescribed; and
	(d)	comply with any other requirements that are prescribed.
	(2)	A local government that receives an application may require the applicant to give the local government, within a specified time, any document or information that the local government requires to determine the application and may require the applicant to verify the information by statutory declaration.
	(3)	The local government may refuse to consider an application if the applicant does not comply with a requirement under subsection (2) within the specified time.
	[Section 54A inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54B.	Record of approval
	(1)	As soon as practicable after a local government makes a decision to grant or refuse to grant an approval to breed or a pet shop approval, or to renew or refuse to renew a pet shop approval, the local government is to enter the decision and the prescribed information in the centralised registration system.
	(2)	A local government is to ensure that the information recorded under subsection (1) is updated to reflect —
	(a)	any change to the information notified under section 54C; and
	(b)	any imposition or amendment of conditions on the approval to breed or pet shop approval; and
	(c)	any expiry or cancellation of the approval to breed or pet shop approval; and
	(d)	the outcome of any objection or review under section 54G or 54H.
	[Section 54B inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54C.	Notice of change to information
		The holder of an approval to breed or a pet shop approval must, within 7 days after the day on which the holder becomes aware of a change to any of the information prescribed under section 54B(1) in respect of the approval, give notice in writing of the change to the local government that granted the approval.
	Penalty: a fine of $5 000.
	[Section 54C inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54D.	Certificate and unique number to be given to holder of approval
	(1)	If a local government grants an approval to breed or a pet shop approval to a person, the local government must —
	(a)	give the person a certificate containing the prescribed information; and
	(b)	in the case of a pet shop approval — issue the person with a unique number for the pet shop to which the approval relates (a pet shop number).
	(2)	If a local government renews a pet shop approval held by a person, the local government must give the person a certificate containing the prescribed information.
	(3)	A local government may give a person who holds an approval to breed or a pet shop approval granted by the local government a new certificate if the local government is satisfied that the person’s certificate has been stolen, lost, damaged or destroyed.
	[Section 54D inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]
Subdivision 2 — Objection and review process
	[Heading inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54E.	Notice of certain decisions made by local government
	(1)	This section applies to each of the following —
	(a)	a decision to refuse to grant an approval to breed;
	(b)	a decision to refuse to grant or renew a pet shop approval;
	(c)	a decision to cancel an approval to breed or a pet shop approval (other than a decision to cancel the approval at the request of the person who held the approval);
	(d)	a decision to impose or amend conditions on an approval to breed or a pet shop approval.
	(2)	Within 7 days after the day on which a local government makes a decision referred to in subsection (1), the local government is to give to the applicant for, or holder of, the approval to which the decision relates written notice of —
	(a)	the decision; and
	(b)	the reasons for the decision; and
	(c)	the person’s rights under sections 54F and 54H either —
	(i)	to lodge a written objection against the decision with the local government, with a subsequent right to apply to the State Administrative Tribunal for a review of the decision made by the local government on the objection; or
	(ii)	to apply directly to the State Administrative Tribunal for a review of the decision.
	[Section 54E inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54F.	Objection may be lodged
	(1)	A person who has been given notice under section 54E of a decision by a local government may, within 28 days after the day on which the person was given the notice, object in writing to the decision.
	(2)	The objection is made by preparing it in a form approved by the CEO and containing the information prescribed, and lodging it with the local government in a manner approved by the local government.
	(3)	Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has applied for a review of the decision under section 54H.
	[Section 54F inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54G.	Dealing with objection
	(1)	The objection is to be dealt with by the council of the local government or by a committee authorised by the council to deal with the objection.
	(2)	A committee cannot deal with an objection against a decision that the committee made or a decision that the council made.
	(3)	The person who made the objection is to be given a reasonable opportunity to make submissions on how to dispose of the objection.
	(4)	The objection may be disposed of by —
	(a)	dismissing the objection; or
	(b)	varying the decision objected to; or
	(c)	revoking the decision objected to, with or without substituting for it another decision.
	(5)	The local government is to ensure that the person who made the objection is given notice in writing of how it has been decided to dispose of the objection and the reasons for disposing of it in that way.
	[Section 54G inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54H.	Review of decisions
	(1)	A person who has been given notice under section 54E of a decision by a local government may apply to the State Administrative Tribunal for a review of the decision if the person —
	(a)	has not lodged an objection to the decision under section 54F; or
	(b)	has lodged an objection but, at the expiration of 35 days after the day on which the objection was lodged, has not been given notice in writing of how it has been decided to dispose of the objection.
	(2)	An application under subsection (1) must be made —
	(a)	if subsection (1)(a) applies — within 42 days after the day on which the person is given the notice under section 54E; or
	(b)	if subsection (1)(b) applies — more than 35 days, but within 77 days, after the day on which the person lodged the objection.
	(3)	If the person lodged an objection and has been given notice in writing of how it has been decided to dispose of the objection, the person may apply to the State Administrative Tribunal, within 42 days after the day on which the person was given the notice, for a review of the decision on the objection.
	[Section 54H inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

54I.	Suspension of effect of some decisions
	(1)	This section applies if —
	(a)	a decision has been made to —
	(i)	cancel an approval to breed or a pet shop approval (other than at the request of the person who held the approval); or
	(ii)	not renew a pet shop approval;
		or
	(b)	a decision has been made under section 54G to dispose of an objection in a way that results in —
	(i)	an approval to breed or a pet shop approval being cancelled; or
	(ii)	a pet shop approval not being renewed.
	(2)	The effect of the decision is suspended, and the approval is taken to continue to have effect, until —
	(a)	if an application is made to the State Administrative Tribunal under section 54H for a review of the decision — the State Administrative Tribunal determines the application; or
	(b)	in any other case — there is no longer any right to lodge an objection under section 54F or apply to the State Administrative Tribunal under section 54H in relation to the decision.
	(3)	Subsection (2) does not apply if the State Administrative Tribunal orders that the effect of the decision should not be suspended.
	[Section 54I inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 42.]

55.	Application of Interpretation Act 1984
		The provisions of this Division do not prejudice or affect the application of the Interpretation Act 1984 to and in relation to the repeals of provisions of the Dog Act 1976 effected by the Dog Amendment Act 2013.
	[Section 55 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

56.	Authorisations in relation to assistance dogs
		A dog specified in an authority given by the Minister under the Dog Act 1976 section 8 and in effect immediately before the day on which the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 7 comes into operation is, on and from that day, to be taken to be an assistance dog as defined in the Dog Act 1976 section 8(1) as inserted by the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 7.
	[Section 56 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

57.	Registration procedure
		An application for registration delivered under the Dog Act 1976 section 16(1) but not finally dealt with under section 16(2) of that Act before the day on which the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 14 comes into operation is, on and from that day, to be dealt with as if the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 14 had not been enacted.
	[Section 57 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

58.	Detained dogs
		A dog that is being detained by or on behalf of a local government immediately before the day on which the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 25 comes into operation, having been seized under the Dog Act 1976 section 29(3) is, on and from that day, to be dealt with as if the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 25 had not been enacted.
	[Section 58 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

59.	Dogs declared to be dangerous dogs
		A declaration under the Dog Act 1976 section 33E(1) that is in effect immediately before the day on which the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 34 comes into operation is, on and from that day, to be taken to be a declaration under the Dog Act 1976 section 33E(1) as amended by the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 34 but any order imposed by the notice given under the Dog Act 1976 section 33F(1) ceases to have effect.
	[Section 59 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

60.	Transitional regulations
	(1)	In this section —
	commencement day means —
	(a)	in the case of transitional regulations under subsection (2)(a) — the day on which the Dog Amendment Act 2013 section 59 commences; or
	(b)	in the case of transitional regulations under subsection (2)(b) — the day on which the amending provision commences;
	Gazettal day means the day on which transitional regulations are published in the Gazette;
	transitional matter means a matter of a transitional, savings or application nature;
	transitional regulations means regulations under subsection (2).
	(2)	Regulations may prescribe anything else required, necessary or convenient to be prescribed in relation to a transitional matter in connection with —
	(a)	the enactment of the Dog Amendment Act 2013; or
	(b)	an amendment made to the Dog Amendment Act 2013 by a provision of another Act (the amending provision).
	(3)	Transitional regulations can only be made before the end of the period of 12 months beginning on commencement day.
	(4)	If transitional regulations provide that a state of affairs is to be taken to have existed, or not to have existed, on and from a day (the operative day) that is earlier than Gazettal day, the regulations have effect according to their terms as long as the operative day is not earlier than commencement day.
	(5)	If transitional regulations contain a provision mentioned in subsection (4), the provision does not operate so as to —
	(a)	affect in a manner prejudicial to any person, other than the State or an authority of the State, the rights of that person existing before Gazettal day; or
	(b)	impose liabilities on any person, other than the State or an authority of the State, in respect of anything done or omitted to be done before Gazettal day.
	[Section 60 inserted: No. 18 of 2013 s. 59.]

61.	Authorised persons
	(1)	This section applies to a person who, immediately before the day on which the Local Government Legislation Amendment Act 2019 section 109 comes into operation, was a person appointed under section 29(1).
	(2)	The person is taken to be an authorised person appointed under the Local Government Act 1995 section 9.10(2) for the purposes of this Act on the terms and conditions that were applicable to the person’s appointment under section 29(1) immediately before the day referred to in subsection (1).

62.	Transitional provision for centralised registration system
	(1)	In this section —
	centralised registration system means the electronic database or system the CEO will be required to establish and maintain when the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 14 comes into operation;
	commencement day means the day on which the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 14 comes into operation.
	(2)	The CEO may establish and maintain the centralised registration system before the commencement day and may —
	(a)	permit a local government to record in the centralised registration system any information that the local government is required under this Act to record in a register maintained by it; and
	(b)	cause or permit information to be transferred from a register maintained by a local government to the centralised registration system.
	(3)	If a local government records information in the centralised registration system under subsection (2)(a), or information from a register maintained by the local government is transferred to the centralised registration system under subsection (2)(b), before the commencement day the information is taken, for the purposes of this Act, to be information recorded by the local government on a register maintained by the local government.
	[Section 62 inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 44.]

63.	Registered unsterilised dogs
	(1)	In this section —
	commencement day means the day on which the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 16 comes into operation.
	(2)	If the registration of a dog that is not sterilised is, at the time immediately before the commencement day, in effect under this Act, section 15, as it is immediately before the commencement day, continues to apply to the registration (until the registration ceases to have effect in accordance with that section) as if the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 16 had not been enacted.
	[Section 63 inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 45.]

64.	Application for registration
		An application for registration delivered under section 16(1) but not finally dealt with under section 16(2) before the day on which the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 17 comes into operation is, on and from that day, to be dealt with as if the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 17(5) had not been enacted.
	[Section 64 inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 45.]

65.	Transition period for relevant pet shop businesses
	(1)	In this section —
	application day means the prescribed date;
	commencement day means the day on which the Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 section 32 comes into operation;
	preexisting dog, in relation to a relevant pet shop business, means a dog that is supplied to the relevant pet shop business (within the meaning of section 38A) before the application day.
	(2)	If, immediately before the commencement day, a person conducts a relevant pet shop business —
	(a)	sections 38B, 38G, 38H, 38I, 38J, 38K and 38L do not apply to the person in relation to the relevant pet shop business and the pet shop before the application day; and
	(b)	sections 38G, 38I, 38J, 38K and 38L do not apply to the person in relation to a preexisting dog.
	(3)	Section 38N does not apply to a person before the application day.
	[Section 65 inserted: No. 29 of 2021 s. 45.]

IMPORT prelude

-- =============================================================================
-- Dog Act 1976 (Western Australia) -- Dog attacks and dangerous dogs
--
-- Isomorphic encoding of s. 3 (extract, the defined terms this file reads)
-- and Part VI Division 1 s. 33D ("Dog attacks etc.") and Division 2
-- ("Dangerous dogs", ss 33E-33M), as at the compilation dated 28 Nov 2024
-- [version 08-b0-00], re-verified current 2026-09-09.
--
-- Source, provenance and scope: source-s33.txt (this directory) and
-- sources/source-bundle.json. External-modification sweep:
-- sources/external-modifications.json. Ambiguity register:
-- sources/fork-register.json. Five ambiguities were found; one
-- (F-DANGEROUS-DOG-STATUS-TIMING) is materialised below as the
-- `Interpretation` record's `dangerousDogStatusTiming` field.
--
-- SCOPED OUT (cited at their site with @ref, never expanded): s. 15
-- (registration fees), s. 22 ("the relevant day" for microchipping), s. 29
-- (power to seize dogs generally), s. 30(3) (working-dog exemption), s. 31(2B)
-- (place declarations), Interpretation Act 1984 s. 71 (continuing/further
-- offences -- recorded as a bare per-further-offence NUMBER, not computed).
-- =============================================================================

§ `3. Terms used (extract)`

DECLARE LiableParty HAS
    `is the registered owner of the dog`                                                      IS A BOOLEAN
    `is the owner of the dog`                                                                  IS A BOOLEAN
    `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live` IS A BOOLEAN
    `has the dog in possession or under control`                                               IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a veterinarian, or acting on a veterinarian's behalf, in professional practice`         IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a police officer or other person acting under statutory duty or administering this Act` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "person liable for the control of the dog"
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the party is a person liable for the control of the dog` party MEANS
        (   party's `is the registered owner of the dog`
         OR party's `is the owner of the dog`
         OR party's `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live`
         OR party's `has the dog in possession or under control`)
    AND NOT party's `is a veterinarian, or acting on a veterinarian's behalf, in professional practice`
    AND NOT party's `is a police officer or other person acting under statutory duty or administering this Act`

DECLARE DogProfile HAS
    `declared to be a dangerous dog (declared) under s 33E(1)` IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a commercial security dog`                             IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "dangerous dog"
GIVEN dog IS A DogProfile
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog is a dangerous dog` dog MEANS
        dog's `declared to be a dangerous dog (declared) under s 33E(1)`
    OR  dog's `is a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`
    OR  dog's `is a commercial security dog`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "attack"
-- AMBIGUITY (F-ATTACK-PROVOCATION-UNLESS): "does not include behaviour...
-- induced by provocation, but includes (a)-(d)..., unless the owner
-- establishes...reasonable cause". Taken reading: the provocation exclusion
-- is a categorical carve-out; "unless...reasonable cause" qualifies only the
-- (a)-(d) inclusion list. Rejected: the "unless" clause reopening the whole
-- definition, including the provocation exclusion itself. See
-- sources/fork-register.json entry F-ATTACK-PROVOCATION-UNLESS.
DECLARE AttackFacts HAS
    `behaviour was an immediate response to, and induced by, provocation` IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour aggressively rushed at or harassed a person or animal`     IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour bit or otherwise caused physical injury`                  IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour tore clothing or caused damage to property`               IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour was an attempt to attack, or would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner establishes the behaviour was justified by a reasonable cause` IS A BOOLEAN

GIVEN facts IS AN AttackFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the behaviour is an attack` facts MEANS
    IF facts's `behaviour was an immediate response to, and induced by, provocation`
    THEN FALSE
    ELSE
            (   facts's `behaviour aggressively rushed at or harassed a person or animal`
             OR facts's `behaviour bit or otherwise caused physical injury`
             OR facts's `behaviour tore clothing or caused damage to property`
             OR facts's `behaviour was an attempt to attack, or would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury`)
        AND NOT facts's `owner establishes the behaviour was justified by a reasonable cause`

-- Penalty: a shared shape for every fine/minimum/imprisonment/further-offence
-- limb in ss 33D and 33E-33M. `fine` and `imprisonment months` are MAYBE
-- NUMBER (not NUMBER 0) because s 33GA(11)'s crime carries imprisonment with
-- no fine at all, and several limbs carry no minimum and no further-offence
-- add-on -- absence is a different fact from a zero.
DECLARE Penalty HAS
    fine                     IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `minimum fine`           IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `imprisonment months`    IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `further offence fine`  IS A MAYBE NUMBER
        @ref Interpretation Act 1984 s. 71 -- "further offence" multiplier not computed; scoped out

-- The recurring $10,000 / $500 minimum / $500 further-offence shape: ss
-- 33GA(1),(2),(4),(5),(6),(7),(8),(9); 33GB(1); 33K(1),(2),(3),(4),(5A).
`standard dangerous dog offence penalty` MEANS
    Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 500, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS JUST 500

-- The recurring $10,000 / $500 minimum, no further-offence shape: ss
-- 33GC(2),(3),(4),(5); 33GD; 33GE(2).
`dangerous dog transfer offence penalty` MEANS
    Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 500, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

§ `Interpretation -- materialised ambiguity`

-- R4: fork F-DANGEROUS-DOG-STATUS-TIMING (sources/fork-register.json) is
-- materialised as this field. Taken reading: statusAtTimeOfOffence.
DECLARE DangerousDogStatusTiming IS ONE OF
    statusAtTimeOfOffence
    statusAtTimeOfProsecution

DECLARE Interpretation HAS
    dangerousDogStatusTiming IS A DangerousDogStatusTiming

§ `Part VI, Division 1 -- Dogs generally`
§§ `33D. Dog attacks etc.`

DECLARE AttackIncident HAS
    `the behaviour is an attack (s 3)`                             IS A BOOLEAN
    `physical injury was caused to the person or animal`           IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog's dangerous-dog status at the time of this offence`       IS A DogProfile
    `dog's dangerous-dog status now`                                IS A DogProfile

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D Penalty limbs; F-DANGEROUS-DOG-STATUS-TIMING
GIVEN incident IS AN AttackIncident, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog counted as a dangerous dog for a s 33D penalty` incident interp MEANS
    CONSIDER interp's dangerousDogStatusTiming
    WHEN statusAtTimeOfOffence    THEN `the dog is a dangerous dog` (incident's `dog's dangerous-dog status at the time of this offence`)
    WHEN statusAtTimeOfProsecution THEN `the dog is a dangerous dog` (incident's `dog's dangerous-dog status now`)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(1)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty, incident IS AN AttackIncident
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 33D(1) offence -- attack or chase causing physical injury` party incident MEANS
        `the party is a person liable for the control of the dog` party
    AND incident's `the behaviour is an attack (s 3)`
    AND incident's `physical injury was caused to the person or animal`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(1) Penalty
GIVEN incident IS AN AttackIncident, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A Penalty
`s 33D(1) penalty` incident interp MEANS
    IF `the dog counted as a dangerous dog for a s 33D penalty` incident interp
    THEN Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 20_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 1_000, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING
    ELSE Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS NOTHING,    `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(2A)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty, incident IS AN AttackIncident
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 33D(2A) offence -- attack or chase without physical injury` party incident MEANS
        `the party is a person liable for the control of the dog` party
    AND incident's `the behaviour is an attack (s 3)`
    AND NOT incident's `physical injury was caused to the person or animal`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(2A) Penalty
GIVEN incident IS AN AttackIncident, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A Penalty
`s 33D(2A) penalty` incident interp MEANS
    IF `the dog counted as a dangerous dog for a s 33D penalty` incident interp
    THEN Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 500, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING
    ELSE Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 3_000,  `minimum fine` IS NOTHING,  `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

DECLARE AttackDefenceFacts HAS
    `dog used in good faith in reasonable defence of a person or property, or for droving/removal of a trespassing animal` IS A BOOLEAN
    `charged person is the occupier where the dog is ordinarily kept or permitted to live, and the dog was owned by an identified adult` IS A BOOLEAN
    `charged person is the owner, and the dog was in another person's possession or control without the owner's consent` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(2B)
GIVEN d IS AN AttackDefenceFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a s 33D(1)/(2A) defence is established` d MEANS
        d's `dog used in good faith in reasonable defence of a person or property, or for droving/removal of a trespassing animal`
    OR  d's `charged person is the occupier where the dog is ordinarily kept or permitted to live, and the dog was owned by an identified adult`
    OR  d's `charged person is the owner, and the dog was in another person's possession or control without the owner's consent`

DECLARE SettingOnFacts HAS
    `person set on or urged the dog to attack or chase a person or animal`             IS A BOOLEAN
    `done in good faith in the reasonable defence of a person or property`             IS A BOOLEAN
    `done in good faith for the droving or removal of a trespassing or consented-to animal` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(2)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty, f IS A SettingOnFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 33D(2) offence -- setting on or urging a dog to attack` party f MEANS
        `the party is a person liable for the control of the dog` party
    AND f's `person set on or urged the dog to attack or chase a person or animal`
    AND NOT (   f's `done in good faith in the reasonable defence of a person or property`
             OR f's `done in good faith for the droving or removal of a trespassing or consented-to animal`)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33D(2) Penalty
GIVEN incident IS AN AttackIncident, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A Penalty
`s 33D(2) penalty` incident interp MEANS
    IF `the dog counted as a dangerous dog for a s 33D penalty` incident interp
    THEN Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 20_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 1_000, `imprisonment months` IS JUST 24, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING
    ELSE Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS NOTHING,    `imprisonment months` IS JUST 12, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

-- s 33D(3) -- saving clause: this section does not affect the duty under The
-- Criminal Code s 266(2), or that Code's Chapter XXVIII/XXIX, or any other
-- law about the consequences of failing that duty. Not a computed rule --
-- there is no fact this encoding derives from a saving clause -- so it is
-- recorded here as inert prose, per the scope note above.

§ `Part VI, Division 2 -- Dangerous dogs`
§§ `33E. Individual dog may be declared to be dangerous dog (declared)`

-- AMBIGUITY (F-REPEATEDLY-TENDENCY): "repeatedly" (s 33E(1)(b)) is
-- undefined. Delegated to the declaring local government's/authorised
-- person's own certified opinion, per s 33E(1)'s own "in the opinion of"
-- language. See sources/fork-register.json entry F-REPEATEDLY-TENDENCY.
DECLARE DeclarationGrounds HAS
    `dog has caused injury or damage by an attack on, or chasing, a person, animal or vehicle` IS A BOOLEAN

    `dog has repeatedly shown a tendency to threaten to attack`                                 IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour meets other criteria prescribed for the purpose of s 33E`                        IS A BOOLEAN
    `s 30(3) working-dog exemption applies to this behaviour`                                   IS A BOOLEAN

-- determination of a lodged objection within 35 days, the owner gains an

-- Dog Act 1976 (Western Australia) -- shared domain module
--
-- The genuinely cross-cutting building blocks from s. 3 "Terms used" that
-- more than one part of this Act's encoding reads: who counts as a "person
-- liable for the control of the dog", what "dangerous dog" and "attack"
-- mean, and the shared shape of a statutory Penalty. Every other module in
-- this corpus IMPORTs this one rather than re-declaring these.
--
-- Deliberately NOT here: the DogActParty/DogActAction regulative-rule types
-- and any dollar-amount Penalty presets. L4 sum types cannot be extended
-- across modules, and the Act's remaining Parts introduce enough distinct
-- actors (CEO, Minister, Registration Officer, State Administrative
-- Tribunal, pet shop operators, ...) and distinct penalty amounts that
-- forcing them through one shared enum or one shared preset would be a
-- false economy -- each module declares its own, scoped to what it needs.
-- =============================================================================

§ `3. Terms used (extract, cross-cutting)`

DECLARE LiableParty HAS
    `is the registered owner of the dog`                                                      IS A BOOLEAN
    `is the owner of the dog`                                                                  IS A BOOLEAN
    `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live` IS A BOOLEAN
    `has the dog in possession or under control`                                               IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a veterinarian, or acting on a veterinarian's behalf, in professional practice`         IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a police officer or other person acting under statutory duty or administering this Act` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "person liable for the control of the dog"
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the party is a person liable for the control of the dog` party MEANS
        (   party's `is the registered owner of the dog`
         OR party's `is the owner of the dog`
         OR party's `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live`
         OR party's `has the dog in possession or under control`)
    AND NOT party's `is a veterinarian, or acting on a veterinarian's behalf, in professional practice`
    AND NOT party's `is a police officer or other person acting under statutory duty or administering this Act`

DECLARE DogProfile HAS
    `declared to be a dangerous dog (declared) under s 33E(1)` IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `is a commercial security dog`                             IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "dangerous dog"
GIVEN dog IS A DogProfile
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog is a dangerous dog` dog MEANS
        dog's `declared to be a dangerous dog (declared) under s 33E(1)`
    OR  dog's `is a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`
    OR  dog's `is a commercial security dog`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "attack"
-- AMBIGUITY (F-ATTACK-PROVOCATION-UNLESS): "does not include behaviour...
-- induced by provocation, but includes (a)-(d)..., unless the owner
-- establishes...reasonable cause". Taken reading: the provocation exclusion
-- is a categorical carve-out; "unless...reasonable cause" qualifies only the
-- (a)-(d) inclusion list. Rejected: the "unless" clause reopening the whole
-- definition, including the provocation exclusion itself. See
-- sources/fork-register.json entry F-ATTACK-PROVOCATION-UNLESS.
DECLARE AttackFacts HAS
    `behaviour was an immediate response to, and induced by, provocation` IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour aggressively rushed at or harassed a person or animal`     IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour bit or otherwise caused physical injury`                  IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour tore clothing or caused damage to property`               IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour was an attempt to attack, or would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner establishes the behaviour was justified by a reasonable cause` IS A BOOLEAN

GIVEN facts IS AN AttackFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the behaviour is an attack` facts MEANS
    IF facts's `behaviour was an immediate response to, and induced by, provocation`
    THEN FALSE
    ELSE
            (   facts's `behaviour aggressively rushed at or harassed a person or animal`
             OR facts's `behaviour bit or otherwise caused physical injury`
             OR facts's `behaviour tore clothing or caused damage to property`
             OR facts's `behaviour was an attempt to attack, or would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury`)
        AND NOT facts's `owner establishes the behaviour was justified by a reasonable cause`

-- Penalty: the shared shape for every fine/minimum/imprisonment/further-offence
-- limb across the Act. `fine` and `imprisonment months` are MAYBE NUMBER
-- (not NUMBER 0) because some crimes carry imprisonment with no fine at all,
-- and many limbs carry no minimum and no further-offence add-on -- absence
-- is a different fact from a zero. Modules construct their OWN dollar-amount
-- presets; none are declared here.
DECLARE Penalty HAS
    fine                    IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `minimum fine`          IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `imprisonment months`   IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `further offence fine`  IS A MAYBE NUMBER
        -- @ref Interpretation Act 1984 s. 71 -- "further offence" multiplier not computed; scoped out

DECLARE `S54I Trigger` HAS

    `decision made not to renew a pet shop approval`                                                                                          IS A BOOLEAN
    `decision made under s 54G to dispose of an objection in a way resulting in the approval to breed or pet shop approval being cancelled`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `decision made under s 54G to dispose of an objection in a way resulting in a pet shop approval not being renewed`                        IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 54I(1)
GIVEN t IS A `S54I Trigger`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 54I applies to the decision` t MEANS
        t's `decision made to cancel an approval to breed or a pet shop approval, other than at the holder's own request`
    OR  t's `decision made not to renew a pet shop approval`
    OR  t's `decision made under s 54G to dispose of an objection in a way resulting in the approval to breed or pet shop approval being cancelled`
    OR  t's `decision made under s 54G to dispose of an objection in a way resulting in a pet shop approval not being renewed`

-- s 54I(2)(b)'s "no longer any right to lodge an objection under s 54F or
-- apply to SAT under s 54H" is left as a single fact-supplied BOOLEAN
-- rather than re-derived from the s 54F/54H predicates above: doing so
-- would require threading the s 54E-notice clock, the s 54F objection
-- clock and the s 54H application clock all the way through this record,
-- for a fact this section only ever consumes as a yes/no gate. Not a
-- statutory ambiguity -- an encoding-economy choice, noted for the record.
DECLARE `S54I Status` HAS
    `an application has been made to SAT under s 54H for a review of the decision`                                            IS A BOOLEAN
    `SAT has determined that application`                                                                                      IS A BOOLEAN
    `there is no longer any right to lodge an objection under s 54F or apply to SAT under s 54H in relation to the decision`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `SAT has ordered that the effect of the decision should not be suspended`                                                  IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 54I(2)-(3)
GIVEN t IS A `S54I Trigger`, s IS A `S54I Status`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the effect of the decision is suspended, and the approval continues to have effect, under s 54I` t s MEANS
        `s 54I applies to the decision` t
    AND NOT s's `SAT has ordered that the effect of the decision should not be suspended`
    AND (`review pending` OR `still within time to object or apply for review`)
    WHERE
        `review pending` MEANS
                s's `an application has been made to SAT under s 54H for a review of the decision`
            AND NOT s's `SAT has determined that application`
        `still within time to object or apply for review` MEANS
                (NOT s's `an application has been made to SAT under s 54H for a review of the decision`)
            AND NOT s's `there is no longer any right to lodge an objection under s 54F or apply to SAT under s 54H in relation to the decision`

§§§ `60. Transitional regulations`

-- s 60(1)'s definitions (commencement day -- two cases, Gazettal day,

-- none of them is read anywhere else in this Part.

-- s 60(2): a discretionary regulation-making POWER ("Regulations may
-- prescribe anything else required, necessary or convenient ... in
-- connection with" the 2013 Act's enactment or a later amending
-- provision) -- not a party's obligation, and no fact a downstream rule in
-- this file tests beyond what s 60(3)-(5) already capture (those sections
-- test properties of regulations made under this power -- their timing,
-- their retrospective terms, their limits -- not whether the power itself
-- was exercised). Recorded as inert prose, on the same footing as s 62(2)
-- below.

DECLARE `S60(3) Facts` HAS
    `months elapsed since commencement day` IS A NUMBER
        -- unit is MONTHS, matching the statute's own "period of 12 months" (this file's

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 60(3)

DECLARE `S60(4) Facts` HAS

DECLARE `S60(5) Facts` HAS
    `person is the State or an authority of the State`                                                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `provision would prejudicially affect this person's rights existing before Gazettal day`               IS A BOOLEAN
    `provision would impose a liability on this person for something done or omitted before Gazettal day` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 60(5)

GIVETH A BOOLEAN

DECLARE `S62(3) Facts` HAS

§ `Part II -- Administration`
§§ `9. Administrative responsibility`

-- s. 9(1): the duty to administer and enforce the Act is not itself a fact
-- another rule would test. The one operative fact in this subsection is the
-- Governor's power, by Order, to deem an outside area to be within a local
-- government's district; that deeming is what downstream jurisdictional
-- questions (e.g. s. 10(2) below) would care about.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9(1)
GIVEN `a s 9(1) Order has been made declaring the area to be within the district for the purposes of this Act` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the area is treated as within the local government's district under s 9(1)` `a s 9(1) Order has been made declaring the area to be within the district for the purposes of this Act` MEANS
    `a s 9(1) Order has been made declaring the area to be within the district for the purposes of this Act`

-- s. 9(2): a savings clause -- nothing in s. 9(1) prevents the CEO from
-- performing the CEO's functions, or from doing anything the CEO considers
-- appropriate for performing them. No fact this Part's rules would test;
-- recorded here as inert prose, per the s. 33D(3) precedent.

§§ `9A. Delegation by CEO`

DECLARE `S9A Delegation` HAS
    `in writing`          IS A BOOLEAN
    `signed by the CEO`   IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9A(1)-(2)
GIVEN d IS A `S9A Delegation`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a s 9A delegation is validly made` d MEANS
    d's `in writing` AND d's `signed by the CEO`

-- s. 9A(3): a person to whom a power or duty is delegated under this section
-- cannot delegate it onward -- an absolute bar, not conditioned on any fact.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9A(3)
`a s 9A delegate may validly sub-delegate the power or duty` MEANS FALSE

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9A(4)
GIVEN `the contrary is shown` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the CEO's delegate is presumed to have acted within the terms of the s 9A delegation` `the contrary is shown` MEANS
    NOT `the contrary is shown`

-- s. 9A(5): the section does not limit the CEO's ability to perform a
-- function through an officer or agent. No fact this Part's rules would
-- test; recorded here as inert prose.

§§ `9B. Designated persons`

DECLARE `S9B Authorisation` HAS
    `made in writing by the CEO`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `cancelled by the CEO`         IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9B(1)
GIVEN a IS A `S9B Authorisation`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a s 9B(1) authorisation is validly made` a MEANS
    a's `made in writing by the CEO`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9B(2)(b)
GIVEN a IS A `S9B Authorisation`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a s 9B authorisation remains in force` a MEANS
    a's `made in writing by the CEO` AND NOT a's `cancelled by the CEO`

-- s. 9B(2)(a) (an authorisation may limit the designated person's functions
-- to those specified) and s. 9B(3) (the CEO is to issue each designated
-- person a certificate) describe the authorisation's optional scope and its
-- evidentiary paper trail; neither is independently tested by any rule in
-- this Part. The certificate's existence is taken as a fact input to the
-- s. 9B(4) duty below rather than separately modelled.

DECLARE `S9B4 Facts` HAS
    `reasonable request made by a person in respect of whom the designated person exercises, has exercised, or is about to exercise a power under this Act` IS A BOOLEAN
    `certificate issued under s 9B(3) is produced in response`                                                                                              IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 9B(4)
GIVEN f IS A `S9B4 Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the designated person complies with the s 9B(4) duty to produce the certificate` f MEANS
        (NOT f's `reasonable request made by a person in respect of whom the designated person exercises, has exercised, or is about to exercise a power under this Act`)
    OR  f's `certificate issued under s 9B(3) is produced in response`

§§ `10A. Payments to veterinarians towards cost of sterilisation`

    `is the registered owner of the dog, whether or not the registration is in the district of the local government or in another district` IS A BOOLEAN
    `resides in the district of the local government`                                                                                        IS A BOOLEAN
    `in the local government's opinion, would suffer hardship in paying the whole of the cost of sterilisation of the dog`                    IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 10A(3)
GIVEN p IS A `S10A Eligible Person`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person is an eligible person for the purposes of s 10A` p MEANS

    AND p's `in the local government's opinion, would suffer hardship in paying the whole of the cost of sterilisation of the dog`

§§ `12A. Entry of premises`

DECLARE `S12A1 Entry Facts` HAS
    `occupier consents to entry`                                                                                                 IS A BOOLEAN
    `premises is where a dog is registered to be, or (in an application for registration) described as, ordinarily kept`         IS A BOOLEAN
    `purpose is to ascertain whether the dog is, or will be, effectively confined`                                               IS A BOOLEAN
    `a dog is reasonably suspected to be in or at the premises`                                                                  IS A BOOLEAN
    `purpose is to ascertain whether that suspected dog is registered for the purposes of s 7(1)`                               IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 7(1) -- scoped out, fact-supplied

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 12A(1)
GIVEN f IS A `S12A1 Entry Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`entry and inspection under s 12A(1) is authorised` f MEANS
    LET `entry serves a permitted s 12A(1) purpose` MEANS
            (f's `premises is where a dog is registered to be, or (in an application for registration) described as, ordinarily kept`
             AND f's `purpose is to ascertain whether the dog is, or will be, effectively confined`)
        OR  (f's `a dog is reasonably suspected to be in or at the premises`
             AND f's `purpose is to ascertain whether that suspected dog is registered for the purposes of s 7(1)`)
    IN
        f's `occupier consents to entry` AND `entry serves a permitted s 12A(1) purpose`

DECLARE `S12A2 Entrant` IS ONE OF
    `Authorised Person`
    `Designated Person`
    `Person Named In The Warrant`

DECLARE `S12A2 Entry Facts` HAS
    `entry is under the authority of a warrant`                                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `entry is with the consent of an occupier who has reached 18 years of age`     IS A BOOLEAN
    `purpose relates to the enforcement of this Act`                               IS A BOOLEAN

-- s. 12A(2A) ("without limiting subsection (2)") clarifies that determining

-- shop approval or a dog supply approval is a purpose relating to the
-- enforcement of this Act. It is an interpretive gloss on `purpose relates
-- to the enforcement of this Act` above, not a fresh gate; the approval
-- machinery it names lies outside this chunk's assigned sections, so it is
-- recorded here as inert prose rather than a separate rule.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 12A(2)-(2A)
GIVEN entrant IS A `S12A2 Entrant`, f IS A `S12A2 Entry Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN

    LET `entry is authorised by warrant or consent` MEANS
        CONSIDER entrant
        WHEN `Person Named In The Warrant` THEN f's `entry is under the authority of a warrant`
        OTHERWISE f's `entry is under the authority of a warrant` OR f's `entry is with the consent of an occupier who has reached 18 years of age`
    IN
        `entry is authorised by warrant or consent` AND f's `purpose relates to the enforcement of this Act`

GIVETH A BOOLEAN

    `a Justice of the Peace is satisfied there are reasonable grounds for issuing a s 12A(2) warrant`

        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) Part VI Division 2 offences -- already encoded in dog-act-1976.l4, scoped out, fact-supplied (not imported here per the workflow's parallel-chunk rule)

    AND f's `an authorised person reasonably suspects a dangerous dog to be at the premises`
    AND f's `entry at a reasonable time`
    AND f's `purpose is to ascertain whether an offence against Part VI Division 2 is being committed`

§ `Part III, Division 2 -- Microchipping`
§§ `21. Microchipping of dogs other than dangerous dogs`

-- AMBIGUITY (F-S21-DANGEROUS-DOG-SCOPE): s. 21's HEADING reads "Microchipping
-- of dogs other than dangerous dogs", but s. 21(1)-(2)'s OPERATIVE text is
-- not textually limited to non-dangerous dogs -- it reads "the owner of a
-- dog must ensure...". Two readings: (A) the heading is descriptive/
-- historical only, and s. 21(1)-(2) applies to EVERY dog, dangerous or not,
-- running concurrently with s. 22's dangerous-dog-specific duty (which
-- carries a materially higher penalty and its own exemption/grace-period
-- mechanics); or (B) the heading substantively confines s. 21 to
-- non-dangerous dogs, so a dangerous dog is governed exclusively by s. 22.
-- Taken: reading (A) -- the operative words control over the heading, and
-- this is corroborated by s. 22(6) itself ("Nothing in subsection (3)
-- affects the operation of section 21(1) or (2) in relation to a
-- particular dog"), which presupposes that s. 21(1)/(2) DOES keep
-- operating for a dog that is within s. 22(3)'s grace-period scope -- a
-- presupposition reading (B) would make redundant. (Registration-refusal
-- grounds elsewhere in this Act, ss. 16(3)(da) and 17A(2)(d) -- outside
-- this chunk -- also list "required under section 21 or 22" as two
-- independent bases, neither displacing the other, which is consistent
-- with (A).) Rejected: reading (B). No dog-type gate is therefore added to
-- the s. 21 predicates below; s. 22's dog-type gate is separate and
-- additional, not a substitute.

    `dog is registered under this Act, or under the law of another State or a Territory, so that its registration was in effect on 31 October 2013` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is microchipped`                                                                                         IS A BOOLEAN

-- (declared)" -- so it is gated here on DogProfile's own s. 33E(1)-declared
-- flag, not on the broader `the dog is a dangerous dog` test used for the
-- offence gate itself. A dangerous dog (restricted breed) or a commercial
-- security dog gets no grace period under s. 22(3), even though both are
-- "dangerous dogs" for the offence gate.
GIVEN dog IS A DogProfile, facts IS A `S22 Facts`, exemption IS A `Microchipping Exemption Facts`, grace IS A `S22(3) Grace Period Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 22(2) offence -- dangerous dog not microchipped` dog facts exemption grace MEANS
        `the dog is a dangerous dog` dog
    AND facts's `after the relevant day`
    AND facts's `dog has reached 3 months of age`
    AND NOT facts's `dog is microchipped`
    AND NOT `the dog is exempt from microchipping` exemption
    AND NOT (   dog's `declared to be a dangerous dog (declared) under s 33E(1)`
             AND `a s 22(3) grace period currently applies to the dog` grace)

`s 22(2) penalty` MEANS
    Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 500, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS JUST 500

-- s. 22(6): confirmed by design above -- the s. 21(1)/(2) offence predicates
-- above never read `grace`, so a s. 22(3) grace period can never excuse
-- non-compliance with s. 21(1) or (2) for the same dog. (This is what makes
-- s. 22(6) a non-vacuous provision under the F-S21-DANGEROUS-DOG-SCOPE
-- taken reading above.)

§§ `23. Notice to be given of microchip information`

DECLARE `Microchipping Act Party` IS ONE OF
    `Dog Owner`
    `Microchip Implanter`
    `Person Who Effected The Transfer`

DECLARE `Microchipping Act Action` IS ONE OF
    `give notice of microchip information to the local government`
    `give notice of prescribed information to the microchip database company`
    `give notice of transfer information to the microchip database company`
    `give notice of a change to registration information to the local government`
    `give notice of a change to microchip database information to the microchip database company`

DECLARE `S23 Notice` HAS
    `states the name of the microchip database company for the dog`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `states the microchip's unique identification number for the dog` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 23(1)
GIVEN n IS A `S23 Notice`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the s 23(1) notice satisfies its content requirements` n MEANS
        n's `states the name of the microchip database company for the dog`
    AND n's `states the microchip's unique identification number for the dog`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 23(1)-(2)
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above).
-- s. 23(2): the duty below does not arise at all if the microchip
-- information has been, or will be, provided with a registration
-- application -- modelled as a gate rather than a further deontic branch,
-- following the "mandatory vs discretionary" IF/ELSE FULFILLED pattern.
GIVEN `information was, or will be, provided with an application to the local government to register the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A DEONTIC `Microchipping Act Party` `Microchipping Act Action`
`s 23(1) notification duty` `information was, or will be, provided with an application to the local government to register the dog` MEANS
    IF `information was, or will be, provided with an application to the local government to register the dog`
    THEN FULFILLED
    ELSE
        PARTY  `Dog Owner`
        MUST   `give notice of microchip information to the local government`
        WITHIN 7
        HENCE  FULFILLED
        LEST   BREACH BY `Dog Owner`
               BECAUSE "the local government of the district where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live was not given notice of the microchip database company and the microchip's unique identification number within 7 days of the microchipping, as s 23(1) requires"

§§ `24. Microchip implanter to give information to microchip database company`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 24
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above).
`s 24 notification duty` MEANS
    PARTY  `Microchip Implanter`
    MUST   `give notice of prescribed information to the microchip database company`
    WITHIN 7
    HENCE  FULFILLED
    LEST   BREACH BY `Microchip Implanter`
           BECAUSE "the microchip database company for the dog was not given the prescribed information, in the form (if any) prescribed, within 7 days after the microchip was implanted, as s 24 requires"

§§ `25. Microchip database company's obligations`

DECLARE `Microchip Database Company Facts` HAS
    `information prescribed under s 24 has been given to the company in respect of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
    `company keeps and maintains that information in its microchip database`                IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 25
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above).
GIVEN f IS A `Microchip Database Company Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 25 offence -- microchip database company fails to keep and maintain prescribed information` f MEANS
        f's `information prescribed under s 24 has been given to the company in respect of the dog`
    AND NOT f's `company keeps and maintains that information in its microchip database`

DECLARE `Microchip Interference Facts` HAS
    `person removed or interfered with a microchip implanted in a dog` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26A

§§ `26B. Transfer of ownership of unmicrochipped dogs`

DECLARE `Unmicrochipped Dog Transfer Facts` HAS
    `ownership of the dog was transferred`                                                                                      IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is not microchipped`                                                                                                   IS A BOOLEAN
    `at the time of the transfer, the person is satisfied that a certificate referred to in s 21(4) or 22(4) applies in respect of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26B(1)-(2)
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above).

GIVEN f IS A `Unmicrochipped Dog Transfer Facts`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26C

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26C
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above).
`s 26C notification duty` MEANS

§ `Part III, Division 3 -- Changes to recorded information`
§§ `26D. Notice to be given of changes to recorded information`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26D(a)
-- Penalty: a fine of $5,000 (see `the standard microchipping/notice offence penalty` above), shared with limb (b) below.
-- s. 14(3) (prescribed particulars recorded on the local government's

GIVEN `there is a change to information prescribed under s 14(3) in respect of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A DEONTIC `Microchipping Act Party` `Microchipping Act Action`
`s 26D(a) notification duty -- change to registration information` `there is a change to information prescribed under s 14(3) in respect of the dog` MEANS
    IF `there is a change to information prescribed under s 14(3) in respect of the dog`

        PARTY  `Dog Owner`
        MUST   `give notice of a change to registration information to the local government`
        WITHIN 7
        HENCE  FULFILLED
        LEST   BREACH BY `Dog Owner`
               BECAUSE "the local government with which the dog is registered was not given notice of the change to registration information within 7 days after the change, as s 26D requires"
    ELSE FULFILLED

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26D(b)
GIVEN `there is a change to information prescribed under s 24 in respect of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A DEONTIC `Microchipping Act Party` `Microchipping Act Action`

    IF `there is a change to information prescribed under s 24 in respect of the dog`

        PARTY  `Dog Owner`
        MUST   `give notice of a change to microchip database information to the microchip database company`
        WITHIN 7
        HENCE  FULFILLED
        LEST   BREACH BY `Dog Owner`
               BECAUSE "the microchip database company for the dog was not given notice of the change to microchip database information within 7 days after the change, as s 26D requires"
    ELSE FULFILLED

§ `Part V -- The keeping of dogs`
§§ `26. Limitation as to numbers`

-- s. 26(1): enabling power. A local government MAY, by local law, limit (a)
-- the number of dogs (>= 3 months of age) kept at premises in its district,
-- or (b) the number of dogs of a specified breed kept there. This is a
-- grant of rule-making power with no fact of its own to test; the CONTENT
-- limits on such a local law are s. 26(2)'s validity predicate below, and
-- the numeric result of exercising the power is what s. 26(4)(a)'s offence
-- reads as a plain NUMBER "the limit applicable to the premises".

DECLARE `Local Law Limit` HAS
    `number specified as the limit`                                                                         IS A NUMBER
    `limit purports to apply to dogs kept at a licensed approved kennel establishment (s 26(2)(c))`          IS A BOOLEAN
    `limit purports to apply to dangerous dogs (declared) or dangerous dogs (restricted breed) (s 26(2)(d))` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26(2)(a)
GIVEN n IS A NUMBER
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the specified limit is one the local law may adopt (2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 only)` n MEANS
        n EQUALS 2
    OR  n EQUALS 3
    OR  n EQUALS 4
    OR  n EQUALS 5
    OR  n EQUALS 6

-- s. 26(2)(b) ("cannot prevent the keeping ... of one or 2 dogs ... and any
-- pup of either of those dogs under that age") is declaratory of the floor
-- (2)(a)'s range already guarantees, and of the fact that a pup under 3
-- months is never counted against the limit at all. Both points are
-- already carried by the range test above and by s. 26(4)(a)'s own
-- "reached 3 months of age" qualifier below, so (b) adds no further,
-- independently-testable constraint of its own.

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26(2)
GIVEN limit IS A `Local Law Limit`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a local law limit under s 26(1) is validly made` limit MEANS
        `the specified limit is one the local law may adopt (2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 only)` (limit's `number specified as the limit`)
    AND NOT limit's `limit purports to apply to dogs kept at a licensed approved kennel establishment (s 26(2)(c))`
    AND NOT limit's `limit purports to apply to dangerous dogs (declared) or dangerous dogs (restricted breed) (s 26(2)(d))`

DECLARE `S26(3) Exemption` HAS
    `local government is satisfied the approved-kennel-establishment provisions need not be applied to these premises`                IS A BOOLEAN
    `number of dogs (reached 3 months of age) the exemption purports to authorise`                                                    IS A NUMBER
    `exemption purports to authorise keeping an underage dog that is not a pup of a dog whose keeping is authorised by the exemption` IS A BOOLEAN

-- s. 26(3)(a) ("may be made subject to conditions") and s. 26(3)(c) ("may
-- be revoked or varied at any time") are permissive powers the local
-- government holds over its own exemption, not restrictions on what a
-- valid exemption may say -- neither yields a fact of the exemption to
-- test, so only (3)(b)'s cap is encoded below.

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 26(3)(b)
GIVEN ex IS A `S26(3) Exemption`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`an exemption under s 26(3) is validly made` ex MEANS
        ex's `local government is satisfied the approved-kennel-establishment provisions need not be applied to these premises`
    AND ex's `number of dogs (reached 3 months of age) the exemption purports to authorise` AT MOST 6

-- AMBIGUITY (F-S26-4-B-DANGEROUS-DOG-CAP): s. 26(4)(b) reads "more than -- (i)
-- 2 dangerous dogs (declared); or (ii) 2 dangerous dogs (restricted
-- breed); or (iii) one of each of those kinds of dangerous dogs, that have
-- reached 3 months of age". Taken reading: limb (iii) bites when BOTH
-- counts individually exceed 1 at the same premises -- the most literal
-- transcription of "more than ... one of each of those kinds", and
-- consistent with the statute's own structure of three independently-
-- violable "or"-joined limbs. Rejected reading: some other combined-total
-- cap (e.g. a single mixed headcount ceiling of 2 dogs regardless of kind)
-- -- nothing in the wording folds declared-count and restricted-count into
-- one sum, and a rule that meant that would more naturally have said "more
-- than 2 dangerous dogs of either or both kinds".

§§ `33. Special provision for greyhounds`

-- s 33(2) modifies s 31 for greyhounds: the s 31(2)(a)/(b) exemptions (dog
-- exercise area, rural leashing area) do not apply; a greyhound is instead
-- exempt from s 31(1) while participating in a licensed race or trial; and a
-- person holding more than 2 greyhounds at one time is conclusively deemed
-- incapable of controlling any of them for s 31(1)(a). Encoded as a
-- standalone eligibility predicate -- the modified version of `s 31(1) or
-- (2A) contravened`/`the dog is exempt from s 31(1) under s 31(2)` for a
-- greyhound -- rather than threaded back into the s 31 offence predicate, to
-- avoid parameter explosion; a full integration would gate that predicate on
-- "dog is a greyhound" and substitute this test. s 33(4) means this test (and
-- s 31 generally) is displaced entirely by Division 2 when the greyhound is
-- itself a dangerous dog.
DECLARE `S33 Greyhound Facts` HAS
    `dog is held by a person, and that person holds 2 or fewer greyhounds at that time` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is securely tethered for a temporary purpose by a chain, cord, leash or harness of sufficient strength not exceeding the prescribed length` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is participating in a greyhound race or trial held under a licence issued under the Racing and Wagering Western Australia Act 2003` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is in or on a vehicle`                                                          IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is being exhibited for show purposes`                                           IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is participating in an obedience trial or classes conducted under the auspices of the Canine Association of Western Australia (Inc.), or a body approved by the local government in whose district the trial or classes are conducted` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is registered as bona fide used in the droving or tending of stock and is being so used, or is going to or returning from a place where it will be or has been so used` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is a foxhound in a pack bona fide engaged in hunting or hound exercise, or in going to or returning from hunting or hound exercise` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is being used for retrieving, duck hunting or other customary sporting purposes` IS A BOOLEAN

§ `Part VI, Division 3 -- Protection of stock; vermin disease and parasite control`
§§ `34. Protection of livestock`

-- s 34(1) -- lawful killing of a dog caught attacking an animal or bird.
DECLARE `S34(1) Facts` HAS
    `person owns, or is for the time being lawfully in charge of, the animal or bird` IS A BOOLEAN
    `person found a dog attacking that animal or bird`                                IS A BOOLEAN
    `there is no other way of stopping the attack`                                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `notice was given to a police officer as soon as is practicable after the shooting or destruction` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 34(1)
GIVEN f IS A `S34(1) Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`shooting or destroying a dog under s 34(1) is lawful` f MEANS
        f's `person owns, or is for the time being lawfully in charge of, the animal or bird`
    AND f's `person found a dog attacking that animal or bird`
    AND f's `there is no other way of stopping the attack`
    AND f's `notice was given to a police officer as soon as is practicable after the shooting or destruction`

-- s 34(2) -- lawful killing of an unaccompanied dog found among confined
-- livestock. "Livestock" is defined, for the whole of s. 34, as horse,
-- cattle, sheep, swine, goats or poultry confined in the enclosed place.
-- Whether the dog's own owner is known or not is stated to be immaterial,
-- so no field carries that fact.
DECLARE `S34(2) Facts` HAS
    `person is the owner or occupier of the enclosed paddock, field, yard or other place confining the livestock, or is acting under that owner's or occupier's authority` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the dog was found within that enclosed place`  IS A BOOLEAN
    `the dog was not accompanied by some person`    IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 34(2)
GIVEN f IS A `S34(2) Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`shooting or destroying a dog under s 34(2) is lawful` f MEANS
        f's `person is the owner or occupier of the enclosed paddock, field, yard or other place confining the livestock, or is acting under that owner's or occupier's authority`
    AND f's `the dog was found within that enclosed place`
    AND f's `the dog was not accompanied by some person`

-- s 34(3) -- an evidentiary provision, not a duty or offence: in a civil or
-- penal proceeding arising from an attack on an animal or bird, or the
-- worrying or chasing of livestock, the stated fact is PRIMA FACIE (i.e.
-- rebuttable) evidence that the person had the dog in possession or under
-- control for the purposes of the s. 3 "person liable for the control of
-- the dog" definition (imported as `LiableParty` / `the party is a person
-- liable for the control of the dog` from dog-act-domain). s 34(3) does not
-- itself redefine or override that s. 3 test -- it only supplies one way of

-- -- so this predicate is encoded standalone rather than by constructing a

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 34(3)
GIVEN `the dog was, immediately before the attack or the worrying or chasing, in company with, or had been seen continuously and closely following, a person` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN

    `the dog was, immediately before the attack or the worrying or chasing, in company with, or had been seen continuously and closely following, a person`

-- under his authority", but the offence sentence at the end of s 34(4)

-- Reading (b): the offence reaches ANY person who lays poison in baits

§ `Part VI, Division 4 -- Control of nuisance`
§§ `38. Nuisance dogs`

-- s 38(1) -- what makes a dog a "nuisance" for the purposes of this
-- section. Three independent, disjunctive grounds; (c)(i)/(ii) are
-- themselves alternatives within the noise-based ground. The specific
-- noise level/method/period and occurrence-count/period are left as
-- fact-supplied booleans -- the section names no particular section of
-- regulations that prescribes them.
DECLARE NuisanceDogFacts HAS
    `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that persistently occurs or continues to such a degree or extent that it unreasonably interferes with the peace, comfort or convenience of any person in any place` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is shown to be allowed to behave consistently in a manner contrary to the general interest of the community`                                                                                                IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that exceeds a prescribed noise level measured by a prescribed method over a prescribed period of time`                                                             IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that exceeds a prescribed number of times of occurrence during or over a prescribed period of time`                                                                 IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(1)
GIVEN f IS A NuisanceDogFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog is a nuisance` f MEANS
        f's `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that persistently occurs or continues to such a degree or extent that it unreasonably interferes with the peace, comfort or convenience of any person in any place`
    OR  f's `dog is shown to be allowed to behave consistently in a manner contrary to the general interest of the community`
    OR  f's `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that exceeds a prescribed noise level measured by a prescribed method over a prescribed period of time`
    OR  f's `dog makes a noise, by barking or otherwise, that exceeds a prescribed number of times of occurrence during or over a prescribed period of time`

-- s 38(2)-(3) -- a complaint lodged with an authorised person is the
-- trigger; if the authorised person is satisfied the dog is a nuisance as
-- alleged, the authorised person MAY (not must) issue an order. Modelled
-- as an eligibility/entitlement predicate for the authority to issue,
-- rather than a regulative rule, because the issuing decision is
-- discretionary and carries no deadline of its own -- the deadline
-- appears only once an order actually issues, in (3)'s "time specified in
-- the order" (encoded at s 38(5) below).
DECLARE NuisanceOrderApplication HAS
    `person lodged a complaint in the prescribed form with an authorised person, alleging that the dog is a nuisance` IS A BOOLEAN
    `authorised person is satisfied that the dog is a nuisance as alleged in the complaint`                            IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(2)-(3)
GIVEN app IS A NuisanceOrderApplication
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the authorised person may issue a nuisance order under s 38(3)` app MEANS
        app's `person lodged a complaint in the prescribed form with an authorised person, alleging that the dog is a nuisance`
    AND app's `authorised person is satisfied that the dog is a nuisance as alleged in the complaint`

-- s 38(4) -- a nuisance order has effect for 6 months after the day it is
-- issued. Unit is MONTHS (not days) by this file's convention, since the
-- statute itself measures the period in months here (contrast s 34's
-- "reasonably necessary" test and the day-counted duties elsewhere in this
-- corpus).
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(4)
GIVEN `months elapsed since the order was issued` IS A NUMBER
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the nuisance order remains in effect` `months elapsed since the order was issued` MEANS
    `months elapsed since the order was issued` AT MOST 6

-- s 38(5) -- the person to whom an order is issued must comply with it,
-- during the period it has effect, by the time specified in the order.
-- Genuine deadline-bearing duty -> regulative rule. The deadline itself is
-- not a fixed statutory number (it is whatever time the order specifies),
-- so it is a GIVEN parameter to the duty, measured in days by this file's
-- convention (matching the day-based WITHIN convention used elsewhere in
-- this corpus's dog-act-1976.l4).
DECLARE NuisanceDogParty IS ONE OF
    `Person To Whom The Nuisance Order Is Issued`
    -- corresponds, per s 38(3), to a "person liable for the control of the
    -- dog" (s 3, imported from dog-act-domain as LiableParty) -- but a
    -- DEONTIC's PARTY must be an enum tag, not a record, so the connection
    -- is documented here rather than typed directly.

DECLARE NuisanceDogAction IS ONE OF
    `prevent the behaviour that is alleged to constitute the nuisance`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(3), (5)
GIVEN `time specified in the order, in days from the day it is issued, by which the behaviour must be prevented` IS A NUMBER
GIVETH A DEONTIC NuisanceDogParty NuisanceDogAction
`s 38(5) compliance duty` `time specified in the order, in days from the day it is issued, by which the behaviour must be prevented` MEANS
    PARTY `Person To Whom The Nuisance Order Is Issued`
    MUST  `prevent the behaviour that is alleged to constitute the nuisance`
    WITHIN `time specified in the order, in days from the day it is issued, by which the behaviour must be prevented`
    HENCE FULFILLED
    LEST  BREACH BY `Person To Whom The Nuisance Order Is Issued`
          BECAUSE "the person did not comply with the nuisance order by the time specified in it, as s 38(5) requires"

-- s 38(5) Penalty -- differs by whether the order relates to a dangerous
-- dog (s. 3, imported as DogProfile / `the dog is a dangerous dog`).
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(5) Penalty
GIVEN dog IS A DogProfile
GIVETH A Penalty
`s 38(5) penalty` dog MEANS
    IF `the dog is a dangerous dog` dog
    THEN Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS JUST 500, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS JUST 500
    ELSE Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 5_000,  `minimum fine` IS NOTHING,  `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

-- s 38(6) -- this section (the whole of s. 38, including the compliance
-- duty and its penalty) does not apply to a dog while it is kept at an
-- establishment licensed as an approved kennel establishment under s. 27
-- (outside this chunk's assigned range -- scoped out, fact-supplied).
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38(6)
GIVEN `the dog is, at the relevant time, kept at an establishment licensed as an approved kennel establishment under s 27` IS A BOOLEAN
    -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 27 -- approved kennel establishment licensing, scoped out, fact-supplied
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38 applies to the dog` `the dog is, at the relevant time, kept at an establishment licensed as an approved kennel establishment under s 27` MEANS
    NOT `the dog is, at the relevant time, kept at an establishment licensed as an approved kennel establishment under s 27`
