§ `Part VIA, Division 1 -- Preliminary`
§§ `38A. Supply of dogs to relevant pet shop businesses`

-- A pure definitional provision ("for the purposes of this Part, a person
-- supplies a dog to a relevant pet shop business if--"): it names a term used
-- by Division 3 (out of scope here) rather than creating an offence itself.
DECLARE `Supply To Pet Shop Facts` HAS
    `the person supplies the dog to the person who conducts the relevant pet shop business, or a person acting on their behalf` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the person who conducts the relevant pet shop business, or the person acting on their behalf, is acting for the purposes of the business` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "relevant pet shop business" -- scoped out, fact-supplied

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38A
GIVEN f IS A `Supply To Pet Shop Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person supplies a dog to a relevant pet shop business (s 38A)` f MEANS
        f's `the person supplies the dog to the person who conducts the relevant pet shop business, or a person acting on their behalf`
    AND f's `the person who conducts the relevant pet shop business, or the person acting on their behalf, is acting for the purposes of the business`

§ `Part VIA, Division 2 -- Approval of pet shop for relevant pet shop business`
§§ `38B. Pet shop for relevant pet shop business must be approved`

DECLARE `Pet Shop Approval Facts` HAS
    `the person conducts a relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "relevant pet shop business" -- scoped out, fact-supplied
    `the person holds a pet shop approval for the pet shop granted by the local government in whose district the pet shop is located` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38B
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Approval Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38B offence -- conducting a relevant pet shop business without an approval` f MEANS
        f's `the person conducts a relevant pet shop business`
    AND NOT f's `the person holds a pet shop approval for the pet shop granted by the local government in whose district the pet shop is located`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38B Penalty
`s 38B penalty` MEANS
    Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 10_000, `minimum fine` IS NOTHING, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

§§ `38C. Application for pet shop approval`

DECLARE `Pet Shop Approval Application Facts` HAS
    `the person intends to conduct a relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the person conducts a relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the application was made in accordance with Part X Division 2` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38C(2); Part X Division 2 -- scoped out, fact-supplied

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38C(1)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Approval Application Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person may apply for a pet shop approval (s 38C(1))` f MEANS
    f's `the person intends to conduct a relevant pet shop business` OR f's `the person conducts a relevant pet shop business`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38C(2)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Approval Application Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the application for a pet shop approval is validly made (s 38C(2))` f MEANS
    f's `the application was made in accordance with Part X Division 2`

§§ `38D. Pet shop approval`

-- Shared standing facts: s. 38D(2)(a)/(c)/(d) are also the first three limbs
-- s. 38E(a) cross-refers back to, and s. 38D(2)(b) (the renewal-only limb)
-- cross-refers forward to s. 38E(c)-(f). One record carries every ground so
-- both sections read off the same underlying facts, mirroring the Act's own
-- cross-referencing rather than duplicating the fields.
DECLARE `Pet Shop Standing Facts` HAS
    `the applicant is a convicted person` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "convicted person" -- scoped out, fact-supplied
    `the facilities that the applicant proposes to use, or uses, to keep dogs for the purposes of the relevant pet shop business do not meet the requirements of any relevant written law` IS A BOOLEAN
    `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38D(2) applies` IS A BOOLEAN
    -- AMBIGUITY (F-PETSHOP-DOES-NOT-NEED-APPROVAL): s 38E(b) "the person
    -- does not need the approval" states no test of its own for when a local
    -- government may be so satisfied (e.g. no longer conducting the
    -- business at that location? at any location? ceased trading?). Taken
    -- reading: a plain fact-supplied boolean, left to the local
    -- government's own satisfaction -- following this corpus's existing
    -- precedent for an undefined satisfaction standard (F-33H-SATISFACTION-
    -- STANDARD in dog-act-1976.l4, s 33H(1)). Rejected: inventing an
    -- objective test (e.g. tied to current business activity) the section
    -- does not state.
    `the person does not need the pet shop approval` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the person has not complied with a condition imposed on the pet shop approval` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the person has not complied with a requirement under this Act or the Animal Welfare Act 2002` IS A BOOLEAN
    `there has been a contravention of this Act or the Animal Welfare Act 2002 in relation to the relevant pet shop business conducted by the person or the pet shop to which the pet shop approval relates` IS A BOOLEAN
    `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38E applies` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38D(2)(a), (c), (d)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`grounds within s 38D(2)(a), (c) or (d) apply to the person` f MEANS
        f's `the applicant is a convicted person`
    OR  f's `the facilities that the applicant proposes to use, or uses, to keep dogs for the purposes of the relevant pet shop business do not meet the requirements of any relevant written law`
    OR  f's `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38D(2) applies`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38E(c), (d), (e), (f)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`grounds within s 38E(c), (d), (e) or (f) apply to the person` f MEANS
        f's `the person has not complied with a condition imposed on the pet shop approval`
    OR  f's `the person has not complied with a requirement under this Act or the Animal Welfare Act 2002`
    OR  f's `there has been a contravention of this Act or the Animal Welfare Act 2002 in relation to the relevant pet shop business conducted by the person or the pet shop to which the pet shop approval relates`
    OR  f's `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38E applies`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38D(2)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`, `this is an application for renewal` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`grounds exist for the local government to refuse to grant or renew the pet shop approval (s 38D(2))` f `this is an application for renewal` MEANS
        `grounds within s 38D(2)(a), (c) or (d) apply to the person` f
    OR  (`this is an application for renewal` AND `grounds within s 38E(c), (d), (e) or (f) apply to the person` f)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38D(1)-(2)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`, `this is an application for renewal` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the local government must grant or renew the pet shop approval (s 38D(1)-(2))` f `this is an application for renewal` MEANS
    NOT (`grounds exist for the local government to refuse to grant or renew the pet shop approval (s 38D(2))` f `this is an application for renewal`)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38D(2)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`, `this is an application for renewal` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the local government may refuse to grant or renew the pet shop approval (s 38D(2))` f `this is an application for renewal` MEANS
    `grounds exist for the local government to refuse to grant or renew the pet shop approval (s 38D(2))` f `this is an application for renewal`

-- s 38D(3)-(4) -- the local government's power to attach, amend or revoke
-- conditions on the approval by written notice. Purely administrative
-- machinery: the only downstream fact this Part tests is whether a
-- condition was complied with (already captured above as
-- `the person has not complied with a condition imposed on the pet shop
-- approval`, feeding s 38E(c)); the power to impose/amend/revoke conditions
-- itself has no further fact a rule in this file would test, so it is
-- recorded here as inert prose rather than a force-fit predicate.

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38D(5)
GIVEN `the date the pet shop approval was granted or renewed` IS A DATE,
      `the date being tested` IS A DATE,
      `the pet shop approval was cancelled earlier under s 38E` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the pet shop approval has effect (s 38D(5))` `the date the pet shop approval was granted or renewed` `the date being tested` `the pet shop approval was cancelled earlier under s 38E` MEANS
        (NOT `the pet shop approval was cancelled earlier under s 38E`)
    AND `the date being tested` AT MOST (`add years` `the date the pet shop approval was granted or renewed` 1)

§§ `38E. Cancellation of pet shop approval`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38E
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Standing Facts`, `the person requests that the local government cancel the pet shop approval` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the local government may cancel the pet shop approval (s 38E)` f `the person requests that the local government cancel the pet shop approval` MEANS
        `the person requests that the local government cancel the pet shop approval`
    OR  `grounds within s 38D(2)(a), (c) or (d) apply to the person` f
    OR  f's `the person does not need the pet shop approval`
    OR  `grounds within s 38E(c), (d), (e) or (f) apply to the person` f

§§ `38F. Continuation of pet shop approval until application for renewal decided`

DECLARE `Pet Shop Approval Continuation Facts` HAS
    `the holder applied for renewal of the pet shop approval before the expiry of the approval` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the local government has renewed the approval` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the local government has given the person notice of its decision to refuse to renew the approval` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38F(1)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Approval Continuation Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38F applies (continuation of pet shop approval pending renewal decision)` f MEANS
        f's `the holder applied for renewal of the pet shop approval before the expiry of the approval`
    AND NOT f's `the local government has renewed the approval`
    AND NOT f's `the local government has given the person notice of its decision to refuse to renew the approval`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38F(2)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Approval Continuation Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the pet shop approval continues to have effect despite expiry (s 38F(2))` f MEANS
    `s 38F applies (continuation of pet shop approval pending renewal decision)` f

§§ `38K. Person conducting relevant pet shop business to keep records relating to source of dogs`

-- s 38K(1) -- a pure definitional provision ("relevant dog ... means each of
-- the following"): the two limbs are DISJUNCTIVE ("each of the following"),
-- so a single dog may satisfy both at once (kept for the business for a
-- while, then later supplied). See the F-38K3B-RETENTION-CUMULATIVE
-- ambiguity below, which turns on exactly this.
DECLARE `Relevant Dog Facts` HAS
    `dog is kept for the purposes of the relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is supplied or offered for supply in the course of the relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(1)
GIVEN dog IS A `Relevant Dog Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog is a relevant dog for the purposes of s 38K` dog MEANS
        dog's `dog is kept for the purposes of the relevant pet shop business`
    OR  dog's `dog is supplied or offered for supply in the course of the relevant pet shop business`

-- REVIEW FIX: s 38K(3)'s chapeau ("The person must keep the record, EVEN IF
-- the person ceases to conduct the relevant pet shop business") explicitly
-- extends the recordkeeping duty (and so the s 38K(5) offence) past
-- cessation -- unlike ss 38G/H/I/J, which have no such extension and so
-- correctly keep the narrower "conducts" actor gate. This record's actor
-- gate therefore mirrors s 38L(1)'s own "conducts or has conducted" wording
-- rather than duplicating the narrower gate used elsewhere in this file.
DECLARE `Pet Shop Recordkeeping Facts` HAS
    `the person conducts or has conducted a relevant pet shop business` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 3 "relevant pet shop business" -- scoped out, fact-supplied
    `at least one relevant dog exists in relation to the person` IS A BOOLEAN
    `a record was kept for each relevant dog, containing the prescribed information including information about the supplier` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the record includes evidence necessary to verify the information` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the record was kept in the prescribed way, if any is prescribed` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the record was kept until the end of the applicable retention period under s 38K(3)(b)` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the record was made within any time prescribed under s 38K(4)` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(2)-(3)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Recordkeeping Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38K(2)-(3) recordkeeping obligation is met` f MEANS
        (NOT f's `at least one relevant dog exists in relation to the person`)
    OR  (   f's `a record was kept for each relevant dog, containing the prescribed information including information about the supplier`
        AND f's `the record includes evidence necessary to verify the information`
        AND f's `the record was kept in the prescribed way, if any is prescribed`
        AND f's `the record was kept until the end of the applicable retention period under s 38K(3)(b)`)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(5)
GIVEN f IS A `Pet Shop Recordkeeping Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38K offence -- failing to comply with recordkeeping requirements` f MEANS
        f's `the person conducts or has conducted a relevant pet shop business`
    AND NOT (   `s 38K(2)-(3) recordkeeping obligation is met` f
             AND f's `the record was made within any time prescribed under s 38K(4)`)

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(5) Penalty
`s 38K penalty` MEANS `pet shop division 3 penalty of` 10_000

-- AMBIGUITY (F-38K3B-RETENTION-CUMULATIVE): s 38K(1) defines "relevant dog"
-- disjunctively -- "each of the following": (a) kept for the business's
-- purposes; (b) supplied or offered for supply -- so a single dog can
-- satisfy both limbs (e.g. kept for the business for a period, then later
-- supplied). s 38K(3)(b) then states the retention deadline as two
-- sub-limbs, (i) and (ii), one per s 38K(1) limb, joined by "and". Question:
-- for a dog that is a relevant dog under BOTH limbs, must the record be kept
-- until the LATER of the two five-year windows (the "and" read
-- cumulatively across the sub-limbs), or does only the sub-limb matching
-- whichever characterisation currently applies govern? Taken reading:
-- cumulative -- retention is required for as long as EITHER applicable
-- sub-period has not yet run, i.e. until the later of the two dates where
-- both limbs apply. Rejected: only the "current" characterisation's
-- sub-limb governs, letting a later characterisation reset or shorten an
-- already-running retention clock. (This mirrors the "and"-joined,
-- per-limb-deadline shape of s 38K(1) itself, which this file's
-- disjunctive `the dog is a relevant dog for the purposes of s 38K` already
-- takes as inclusive-or.)
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(3)(b)
GIVEN `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(a) (kept for the purposes of the business)` IS A BOOLEAN,
      `years elapsed since the dog ceased being kept for those purposes` IS A NUMBER,
      `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(b) (supplied or offered for supply)` IS A BOOLEAN,
      `years elapsed since the dog was supplied or first offered for supply` IS A NUMBER
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person must still retain the s 38K(2) record for this dog` `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(a) (kept for the purposes of the business)` `years elapsed since the dog ceased being kept for those purposes` `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(b) (supplied or offered for supply)` `years elapsed since the dog was supplied or first offered for supply` MEANS
        (   `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(a) (kept for the purposes of the business)`
        AND `years elapsed since the dog ceased being kept for those purposes` LESS THAN 5)
    OR  (   `dog is a relevant dog under s 38K(1)(b) (supplied or offered for supply)`
        AND `years elapsed since the dog was supplied or first offered for supply` LESS THAN 5)

-- s 38K(4)'s duty has no numeric deadline of its own in the Act -- the
-- deadline exists only IF the regulations prescribe one. Modelled as a
-- MAYBE NUMBER input (unit: days, by this file's convention, matching
-- dog-act-1976.l4's s 33K(2)/(3) 24-hour duties): NOTHING when no time is
-- prescribed (no duty arises at all, per the section's own "if" clause),
-- JUST days when one is.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38K(4)
GIVEN `time to make the record, in days, if a time is prescribed under s 38K(4)` IS A MAYBE NUMBER
GIVETH A DEONTIC `Pet Shop Party` `Pet Shop Action`
`s 38K(4) duty to make the record within the prescribed time` `time to make the record, in days, if a time is prescribed under s 38K(4)` MEANS
    CONSIDER `time to make the record, in days, if a time is prescribed under s 38K(4)`
    WHEN NOTHING   THEN FULFILLED
    WHEN JUST days THEN
        PARTY `Person Conducting The Relevant Pet Shop Business`
        MUST  `make the record required by s 38K(2)`
        WITHIN days
        HENCE FULFILLED
        LEST  BREACH BY `Person Conducting The Relevant Pet Shop Business`
              BECAUSE "the record required by s 38K(2) was not made within the time prescribed under s 38K(4)"

§§ `38N. Only holder of dog supply approval may supply dogs to relevant pet shop businesses`

DECLARE `S38N Supply Facts` HAS
    `supplied a dog to a relevant pet shop business`                                              IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is a stray, abandoned, seized or surrendered dog`                                         IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is being kept as part of refuge operations conducted by the supplier`                     IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is being kept in a dog management facility operated by the supplier`                      IS A BOOLEAN
    `supplier holds a dog supply approval`                                                         IS A BOOLEAN
    `supplier obtained, in respect of the dog, a veterinarian's health certificate under s 38N(2)(a)` IS A BOOLEAN
    `supplier provided the pet shop business (or the person acting on its behalf) with a copy of the health certificate` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38N(1)
GIVEN f IS A `S38N Supply Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38N(1) offence -- supplying a dog without a qualifying source and an approval` f MEANS
        f's `supplied a dog to a relevant pet shop business`
    AND NOT (
                f's `dog is a stray, abandoned, seized or surrendered dog`
            AND (f's `dog is being kept as part of refuge operations conducted by the supplier` OR f's `dog is being kept in a dog management facility operated by the supplier`)
            AND f's `supplier holds a dog supply approval`
        )

`s 38N(1) penalty` MEANS `$10,000 fine only penalty`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38N(2)
GIVEN f IS A `S38N Supply Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 38N(2) offence -- supplying a dog without a health certificate having been obtained and given to the pet shop business` f MEANS
        f's `supplied a dog to a relevant pet shop business`
    AND NOT (   f's `supplier obtained, in respect of the dog, a veterinarian's health certificate under s 38N(2)(a)`
             AND f's `supplier provided the pet shop business (or the person acting on its behalf) with a copy of the health certificate`)

`s 38N(2) penalty` MEANS `$5,000 fine only penalty`

§§ `38P. Dog supply approval`

-- s 38P(1): on receiving an application, the CEO is to grant or refuse to
-- grant the approval. Purely procedural machinery (the decision itself);
-- what governs it operatively is the s 38P(2) refusal-grounds test below,
-- so s 38P(1) carries no separate fact for a downstream rule to test.

DECLARE `S38P Refusal Grounds` HAS
    `applicant is a convicted person`                                                                                     IS A BOOLEAN
    `applicant purports to conduct refuge operations, and there are reasonable grounds to suspect the operations are not genuine` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- AMBIGUITY (F-GENUINE-REFUGE-OPERATIONS): "genuine" is undefined.
        -- Delegated wholesale to fact-supply, on the same footing as
        -- "repeatedly" at s 33E(1)(b) (F-REPEATEDLY-TENDENCY in
        -- dog-act-1976.l4) -- an evaluative term with no statutory test of
        -- its own. See ambiguities array.
    `the dog management facility, or the facilities the applicant uses to keep dogs for the refuge operations, do not meet the requirements of a relevant written law` IS A BOOLEAN
    `a local government objects to the grant of the approval`                                                              IS A BOOLEAN
    `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38P(2) applies`                                                       IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38P(2)
GIVEN g IS A `S38P Refusal Grounds`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`grounds exist for the CEO to refuse to grant a dog supply approval` g MEANS
        g's `applicant is a convicted person`
    OR  g's `applicant purports to conduct refuge operations, and there are reasonable grounds to suspect the operations are not genuine`
    OR  g's `the dog management facility, or the facilities the applicant uses to keep dogs for the refuge operations, do not meet the requirements of a relevant written law`
    OR  g's `a local government objects to the grant of the approval`
    OR  g's `a circumstance prescribed for the purposes of s 38P(2) applies`

DECLARE `S38P Conditions Facts` HAS
    `CEO considers the conditions necessary or desirable to impose` IS A BOOLEAN
    `conditions are specified in the approval`                       IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 38P(3)
GIVEN c IS A `S38P Conditions Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the s 38P(3) conditions requirement is satisfied` c MEANS
    c's `CEO considers the conditions necessary or desirable to impose` AND c's `conditions are specified in the approval`

§ `Part VII -- Enforcement`

§§ `39. Dogs causing injury or damage may be destroyed`

-- s 39(1) -- the order a court, or the Magistrates Court, may make. "and the
-- provisions of section 40 apply" (the tail after (b)(ii)) is not a further
-- testable fact: s 40(1)'s own jurisdiction predicate below is triggered
-- independently by "application made for an order for the destruction of the
-- dog" or "destruction may be ordered in the proceedings", so it is not
-- gated on which s 39(1)(a)/(b) order-type was chosen; the tail is recorded
-- here as a cross-reference, not encoded as a separate condition.
DECLARE `S39 Destruction Order` IS ONE OF
    `order that the owner destroy the dog or cause it to be destroyed`
    `order that the dog be destroyed by the local government or authorised person by whom it was seized or is detained under s 29`
    `order that the dog be destroyed by a person specifically authorised by the court`
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 29 -- power to seize/detain generally, scoped out

DECLARE `S39 Application Facts` HAS
    `attack by a dog is shown on the balance of probabilities to have caused injury or damage` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the matter is before a court hearing an offence arising out of that attack` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- named without "application": unlike the three Magistrates Court
        -- limbs below, s 39(1) does not describe this forum as acting "on
        -- the application of" anyone -- it is simply "a court before which
        -- any offence arising out of that attack is heard".
    `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by a local government` IS A BOOLEAN
    `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by an authorised person` IS A BOOLEAN
    `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by a person specifically authorised by a local government for the purposes of s 33E` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 33E -- who counts as specifically authorised, scoped out

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 39(1)
GIVEN f IS A `S39 Application Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`a court or the Magistrates Court may order destruction under s 39(1)` f MEANS
        f's `attack by a dog is shown on the balance of probabilities to have caused injury or damage`
    AND (   f's `the matter is before a court hearing an offence arising out of that attack`
         OR f's `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by a local government`
         OR f's `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by an authorised person`
         OR f's `application is to the Magistrates Court, made by a person specifically authorised by a local government for the purposes of s 33E`)

-- s 39(2)
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 39(2)
GIVEN order IS A `S39 Destruction Order`, `person acting is the person specifically authorised by the court under s 39(1)(b)(ii)` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person may give effect to the s 39 order for destruction` order `person acting is the person specifically authorised by the court under s 39(1)(b)(ii)` MEANS
    CONSIDER order
    WHEN `order that the dog be destroyed by a person specifically authorised by the court` THEN `person acting is the person specifically authorised by the court under s 39(1)(b)(ii)`
    OTHERWISE FALSE

-- s 39(3) -- the court's additional requirements on the owner, and the
-- offence for failing to meet whichever of them the court actually imposed.
DECLARE `S39 Requirement Facts` HAS
    `court has made an order that the dog is to be destroyed` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner required to take specified action, within the period specified in the order, to prevent or reduce the likelihood of the dog causing injury, or to enable effect to be given to the order for destruction` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner complied with that action requirement within the period specified in the order` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner required to pay costs or expenses incurred in relation to the detention or destruction of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
    `owner paid those costs or expenses` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 39(3)
GIVEN r IS A `S39 Requirement Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`s 39(3) offence -- owner fails to comply with the court's requirement` r MEANS
        r's `court has made an order that the dog is to be destroyed`
    AND (`failed the action requirement` OR `failed the costs requirement`)
    WHERE
        `failed the action requirement` MEANS
                r's `owner required to take specified action, within the period specified in the order, to prevent or reduce the likelihood of the dog causing injury, or to enable effect to be given to the order for destruction`
            AND NOT r's `owner complied with that action requirement within the period specified in the order`
        `failed the costs requirement` MEANS
                r's `owner required to pay costs or expenses incurred in relation to the detention or destruction of the dog`
            AND NOT r's `owner paid those costs or expenses`

-- s 39(3) Penalty: a fine of $5 000, single limb -- no stated minimum,
-- imprisonment, or further-offence add-on.
`s 39(3) penalty` MEANS
    Penalty WITH fine IS JUST 5_000, `minimum fine` IS NOTHING, `imprisonment months` IS NOTHING, `further offence fine` IS NOTHING

-- s 39(4) -- attribution of causation across a multi-dog attack.
DECLARE `Multi-Dog Attack Facts` HAS
    `attack by 2 or more dogs is shown on the balance of probabilities to have caused injury or damage` IS A BOOLEAN
    `this dog took part in the attack` IS A BOOLEAN
    `possible to show which of the dogs actually caused the injury or damage` IS A BOOLEAN
        -- s 39(4): immaterial to the outcome below; recorded for fidelity to
        -- "even if it is not possible to show which of those dogs actually
        -- caused that injury or damage" -- deliberately not read.

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 39(4)
GIVEN f IS A `Multi-Dog Attack Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the dog is treated, for the purposes of s 39(1), as having caused the injury or damage` f MEANS
        f's `attack by 2 or more dogs is shown on the balance of probabilities to have caused injury or damage`
    AND f's `this dog took part in the attack`

§§ `40. Destruction of dogs etc.`

-- s 40(1) -- the orders available to whichever of the court or the State
-- Administrative Tribunal is dealing with the proceedings. The eight
-- statutory limbs (a)-(g), less (ea) which carries its own further gate
-- below, are the content the order may carry; a court or tribunal with
-- jurisdiction under s 40(1) may combine any number of them in one order,
-- so they are modelled as an enumerated set of order-contents rather than a
-- single choice.
DECLARE `S40 Order Limb` IS ONE OF
    `order the destruction of the dog`
    `provide that the order shall be remitted in specified circumstances`
    `order the seizure and detention of the dog`
    `order that the dog be controlled, or be controlled in a specified manner`
    `order that the dog be disposed of, or be disposed of in a specified manner`
    `authorise a police officer or a person appointed by the local government to give effect to the order`
    `give all necessary directions to make the order effective`

DECLARE `S40 Jurisdiction Facts` HAS
    `application made for an order for the destruction of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
    `in the proceedings before the court or the State Administrative Tribunal, the destruction of the dog may be ordered` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(1)
GIVEN f IS A `S40 Jurisdiction Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the court or the State Administrative Tribunal has jurisdiction to make orders under s 40(1)` f MEANS
    f's `application made for an order for the destruction of the dog`
    OR f's `in the proceedings before the court or the State Administrative Tribunal, the destruction of the dog may be ordered`

-- s 40(1)(a)-(d), (f)-(g): once jurisdiction under s 40(1) is established,
-- every listed limb is equally available and none is gated on which other
-- limb(s) the court or Tribunal also chooses -- e.g. (c) is available
-- "whether or not an order is made for the destruction of the dog". This is
-- what makes `S40 Order Limb` operative rather than a bare enumeration:
-- availability of any limb reduces to the s 40(1) jurisdiction gate above.
-- (ea) is excluded here -- it carries its own further gate, immediately
-- below.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(1)(a)-(d), (f)-(g)
GIVEN f IS A `S40 Jurisdiction Facts`, limb IS A `S40 Order Limb`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the court or the State Administrative Tribunal may include this limb in a s 40(1) order` f limb MEANS
    `the court or the State Administrative Tribunal has jurisdiction to make orders under s 40(1)` f

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(1)(ea)
GIVEN `dog has been detained under s 29(5b)` IS A BOOLEAN, `order has been made under s 40(1)(c) for the seizure and detention of the dog` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the court or the State Administrative Tribunal may make a cost order under s 40(1)(ea)` `dog has been detained under s 29(5b)` `order has been made under s 40(1)(c) for the seizure and detention of the dog` MEANS
    `dog has been detained under s 29(5b)` OR `order has been made under s 40(1)(c) for the seizure and detention of the dog`
        -- @ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 29(4), (5b) -- scoped out, fact-supplied

-- s 40(2) -- content requirements for the order itself, in the style of the
-- S33F/S33G notice content-checks in dog-act-1976.l4.
DECLARE `S40 Destruction Order Statement` HAS
    `states to whom the order is directed` IS A BOOLEAN
    `states whether or not the order may be remitted, and if so in what circumstances` IS A BOOLEAN
    `states the period within which it is to be put into effect` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(2)
GIVEN n IS A `S40 Destruction Order Statement`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the s 40 destruction order satisfies its content requirements` n MEANS
        n's `states to whom the order is directed`
    AND n's `states whether or not the order may be remitted, and if so in what circumstances`
    AND n's `states the period within which it is to be put into effect`

-- s 40(3) -- manner of execution.
DECLARE `S40 Execution Facts` HAS
    `destruction was effected so far as is practicable without cruelty` IS A BOOLEAN
    `destruction was effected by some speedy means` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(3)
GIVEN f IS A `S40 Execution Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the destruction was effected in accordance with s 40(3)` f MEANS
        f's `destruction was effected so far as is practicable without cruelty`
    AND f's `destruction was effected by some speedy means`

-- s 40(4) -- the order survives a change of ownership or of the dog's
-- whereabouts UNLESS a variation application to the ORIGINAL court or
-- tribunal succeeds. The two "changed circumstances" fields (ownership /
-- location) are the backdrop the subsection names as NOT excusing
-- implementation on their own; they are recorded for fidelity but are not
-- read below -- only the application-and-satisfaction limb is operative.
DECLARE `S40 Variation Facts` HAS
    `ownership of the dog has changed, or is not known` IS A BOOLEAN
    `dog is no longer kept in the area for which the local government is the registration authority` IS A BOOLEAN
    `application made to the court or tribunal that made the original order` IS A BOOLEAN
    `court or tribunal is satisfied the changed circumstances are such that the order may be varied` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(4)
GIVEN f IS A `S40 Variation Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the s 40 order must be implemented notwithstanding the change in circumstances` f MEANS
    NOT (   f's `application made to the court or tribunal that made the original order`
         AND f's `court or tribunal is satisfied the changed circumstances are such that the order may be varied`)

-- s 40(5) -- a duty with no stated deadline and no stated penalty; encoded
-- as the identity predicate this corpus already uses for a bare compliance
-- fact (cf. dog-act-1976.l4's "SAT may order the dog's release to the
-- owner").
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 40(5)
GIVEN `person made provision for the disposal of the dog's carcass` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person complied with the s 40(5) duty to dispose of the carcass` `person made provision for the disposal of the dog's carcass` MEANS `person made provision for the disposal of the dog's carcass`

§§ `41. Indemnity as to destruction of dogs`

DECLARE `S41 Indemnity Facts` HAS
    `measures were lawfully taken for the destruction of a dog under this Act` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 41
GIVEN f IS A `S41 Indemnity Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person is indemnified under s 41 against action, claim, demand or an offence, by reason only of the destruction measures` f MEANS
    f's `measures were lawfully taken for the destruction of a dog under this Act`

§§ `45. Evidentiary provisions`

-- s 45(1)(a): an averment in a prosecution notice of any of these 14 kinds
-- is, without more, evidence of the fact averred. The deeming is
-- unconditional across the whole closed list -- there is no fact for a
-- downstream rule to test beyond "is this averment one of these kinds",
-- which is exactly what the enum's membership already states. Kept as a
-- DECLAREd enum for structural fidelity to the numbered list; no computed
-- BOOLEAN wraps it, per the "purely administrative machinery" carve-out.
DECLARE `S45(1)(a) Averment` IS ONE OF
    `a specified person was the registered owner of the dog at a particular time`            -- (i)
    `the dog was ordinarily kept by a specified person`                                       -- (ii)
    `a specified person had the dog in the person's possession or under the person's control` -- (iii)
    `a specified person was the occupier of premises where the dog was ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live` -- (iv)
    `the dog was not registered`                                                               -- (v)
    `the dog was of a particular breed or was a mix of particular breeds`                      -- (vi)
    `the dog was not sterilised`                                                                -- (vii)
    `the dog was not microchipped`                                                              -- (viii)
    `a specified person's name was recorded as the owner of the dog in a microchip database`   -- (ix)
    `a specified database was a microchip database`                                            -- (x)
    `a specified person or body was a microchip database company in relation to the dog`       -- (xi)
    `the dog had reached 3 months of age`                                                       -- (xii)
    `the dog was under 3 months of age`                                                         -- (xiii)
    `the dog was the pup of a particular dog`                                                    -- (xiv)

-- s 45(1)(b), (2A): of that same broad territory, only these five facts
-- carry a REVERSE onus -- the person making the assertion must prove it,
-- rather than the general rule that the prosecution proves its case. This
-- is the genuinely testable fact, encoded as a checkbox record (drafting
-- pattern: independent flags + a disjunction, not an enum, because a single
-- assertion is being tested for membership in this narrower list).
DECLARE `S45 Reverse-Onus Facts` HAS
    `assertion is that the dog was registered at a particular time`             IS A BOOLEAN
    `assertion is that the dog was sterilised at a particular time`             IS A BOOLEAN
    `assertion is that the dog was microchipped at a particular time`           IS A BOOLEAN
    `assertion is that the dog was under 3 months of age at a particular time`  IS A BOOLEAN
    `assertion is that the dog was not a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`      IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 45(1)(b), (2A)
GIVEN a IS A `S45 Reverse-Onus Facts`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the onus of proving the asserted fact lies on the person making the assertion` a MEANS
        a's `assertion is that the dog was registered at a particular time`
    OR  a's `assertion is that the dog was sterilised at a particular time`
    OR  a's `assertion is that the dog was microchipped at a particular time`
    OR  a's `assertion is that the dog was under 3 months of age at a particular time`
    OR  a's `assertion is that the dog was not a dangerous dog (restricted breed)`

-- s 45(2): a s. 16(6) registration certificate, or a certified copy of a

-- court-procedure deeming rule about the weight of a document, not a fact

-- $10,000; or (b) a regulation made under section 48 or 54." (a) and (b) are
-- parallel alternatives, and the cap clause sits grammatically inside (a)

-- route at the s 45A(1) stage (s 45A(3)'s separate 10%-of-maximum cap on the
-- MODIFIED PENALTY AMOUNT itself still applies regardless of which route
-- (1) is reached through). Rejected: the cap also gates (b). See

§§ `46A. Order to attend dog training course, ban on owning or keeping dogs`

-- s 46A(1)(a)/(b) are jointly exhaustive -- every offence either carries a
-- minimum penalty (Penalty's `minimum fine` is JUST something) or does not
-- -- so the court's power to order a training course is available on ANY
-- conviction; what differs is only whether the order is IN ADDITION to the
-- penalty, or an ALTERNATIVE TO (as well as in addition to) it. That
-- distinction is the fact worth carrying, via the "Total enum over MAYBE"
-- pattern: MAYBE because "not convicted" is a genuine absence of any basis.
DECLARE `Training Course Order Basis` IS ONE OF
    `in addition to the penalty (the offence carries a minimum penalty, s 46A(1)(a))`
    `as an alternative to, or in addition to, the penalty (any other offence, s 46A(1)(b))`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 46A(1)
GIVEN `person was convicted of an offence against this Act` IS A BOOLEAN, penalty IS A Penalty
GIVETH A MAYBE `Training Course Order Basis`
`the basis on which the court may order a dog training course under s 46A(1)` `person was convicted of an offence against this Act` penalty MEANS
    IF NOT `person was convicted of an offence against this Act`
    THEN NOTHING

§ `Part VIII -- Civil remedies, etc.`
§§ `46. Damages`

-- s 46(1) -- saving clause: the conviction of a person under this Act does
-- not affect any right or remedy by civil process of any party arising in
-- relation to the same matter, and this Act does not limit or affect any
-- right, remedy or proceeding under any other Act or at law. Not a computed
-- rule -- there is no fact this encoding derives from a saving clause -- so
-- it is recorded here as inert prose, following dog-act-1976.l4's treatment
-- of s 33D(3).

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 46(5)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the party is deemed to be the owner of the dog under s 46(5)` party MEANS
        party's `has the dog in possession or under control`
    OR  party's `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live`

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 46(2), (5)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the party is liable in damages as owner or deemed owner under s 46` party MEANS
        party's `is the owner of the dog`
    OR  `the party is deemed to be the owner of the dog under s 46(5)` party

DECLARE DamagesHarm HAS
    `injury to a person or animal was inflicted`    IS A BOOLEAN
    `damage to the property of a person was caused` IS A BOOLEAN

-- s 46(3): a party seeking damages under s 46(2) need not show a previous
-- mischievous propensity in the dog, the owner's (or deemed owner's)
-- knowledge of that propensity, or that the injury was attributable to the
-- owner's (or deemed owner's) neglect. This encoding reflects that rule by
-- OMITTING any such fact from DamagesHarm or from the predicate below -- not
-- by a separate computed rule; there is no propensity/knowledge/neglect
-- field anywhere in this file for the predicate to fail to require.
--
-- "subject to any contributory negligence" (s 46(2)) qualifies the QUANTUM
-- of damages recoverable, not eligibility for the claim itself -- this Act
-- states no contributory-negligence apportionment formula, so it is not
-- computed here; a downstream quantum assessment is a fact/computation this
-- encoding does not attempt.
@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 46(2)
GIVEN party IS A LiableParty, attack IS AN AttackFacts, harm IS A DamagesHarm
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the owner is liable in damages under s 46(2)` party attack harm MEANS
        `the party is liable in damages as owner or deemed owner under s 46` party
    AND `the behaviour is an attack` attack
    AND (   harm's `injury to a person or animal was inflicted`
         OR harm's `damage to the property of a person was caused`)

DECLARE PossessionDefenceFacts HAS
    `at the material time, the dog was not in the defendant's possession or control` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the dog was, at that time, in the actual possession or control of some other person, without the defendant's consent (express or implied)` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 46(4)
GIVEN f IS A PossessionDefenceFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the "not in possession or control" defence under s 46(4) is established` f MEANS
        f's `at the material time, the dog was not in the defendant's possession or control`
    AND f's `the dog was, at that time, in the actual possession or control of some other person, without the defendant's consent (express or implied)`

        party's `is the occupier of premises where the dog is ordinarily kept or ordinarily permitted to live`

§§ `47. Veterinary service expenses recoverable from local government`

-- AMBIGUITY (F-S47-REPRESENTATIVE-QUALIFIER-SCOPE): s 47(1) defines
-- "representative" as "(a) a person who is an authorised person by virtue
-- of an appointment or designation ...; or (b) an employee of the local
-- government, who, at the relevant time, is performing a function on
-- behalf of the local government." Limb (a) already carries its own
-- self-contained "who is ..." clause; limb (b) does not repeat "who", and
-- the trailing "who, at the relevant time, is performing a function ..."
-- clause follows the whole two-item list rather than sitting inside (b).
-- Two readings compete: the trailing clause could be a common qualifier on
-- BOTH limbs (matching this Act's own convention elsewhere of a trailing
-- clause closing out a limb list, e.g. s 45(1)'s "... is evidence of that
-- fact" closing an (i)-(xiv) list), or it could attach grammatically to
-- limb (b) alone (the closest antecedent, since (a) needs no further
-- qualification -- it is already a complete "a person who is ..." clause).
-- MATERIALISED below as the `S47 Qualifier Scope`/`Interpretation` fields --
-- the readings diverge on a person appointed under (a) who is not currently
-- performing any function for the local government, witnessed by
-- `` `an authorised officer, off duty` `` in the Illustrations. Taken:
-- the qualifier applies to both limbs (the more natural reading of
-- "representative", and the one consistent with this Act's own drafting
-- convention noted above).
DECLARE `S47 Qualifier Scope` IS ONE OF
    qualifierAppliesToBothLimbs
    qualifierAppliesToLimbBOnly

DECLARE Interpretation HAS
    `s 47(1) qualifier scope` IS A `S47 Qualifier Scope`

DECLARE RepresentativeFacts HAS
    `is an authorised person by virtue of an appointment or designation made by the local government` IS A BOOLEAN
    `is an employee of the local government`                                                          IS A BOOLEAN
    `at the relevant time, is performing a function on behalf of the local government`                IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 47(1) "representative"; F-S47-REPRESENTATIVE-QUALIFIER-SCOPE
GIVEN r IS A RepresentativeFacts, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the person is a representative of the local government (s 47(1))` r interp MEANS
    CONSIDER interp's `s 47(1) qualifier scope`
    WHEN qualifierAppliesToBothLimbs THEN
            (   r's `is an authorised person by virtue of an appointment or designation made by the local government`
             OR r's `is an employee of the local government`)
        AND r's `at the relevant time, is performing a function on behalf of the local government`
    WHEN qualifierAppliesToLimbBOnly THEN
            r's `is an authorised person by virtue of an appointment or designation made by the local government`
        OR  (   r's `is an employee of the local government`
             AND r's `at the relevant time, is performing a function on behalf of the local government`)

DECLARE VetServiceRequest HAS
    `veterinary services were requested in respect of a dog` IS A BOOLEAN
    requester                                                IS A RepresentativeFacts

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 47(2)
GIVEN req IS A VetServiceRequest, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the local government is liable to pay for the veterinary services under s 47(2)` req interp MEANS
        req's `veterinary services were requested in respect of a dog`
    AND `the person is a representative of the local government (s 47(1))` (req's requester) interp

DECLARE VetCostClaim HAS
    `veterinarian provided services in respect of a dog` IS A BOOLEAN
    requester                                            IS A RepresentativeFacts
    `amount of the costs for the services`               IS A NUMBER

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 47(3)
GIVEN c IS A VetCostClaim, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the veterinarian may recover the costs from the local government under s 47(3)` c interp MEANS
        c's `veterinarian provided services in respect of a dog`
    AND `the person is a representative of the local government (s 47(1))` (c's requester) interp

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 47(3)
GIVEN c IS A VetCostClaim, interp IS AN Interpretation
GIVETH A MAYBE NUMBER
`the amount recoverable by the veterinarian under s 47(3)` c interp MEANS
    IF `the veterinarian may recover the costs from the local government under s 47(3)` c interp
    THEN JUST (c's `amount of the costs for the services`)
    ELSE NOTHING

§§ `52. Revocation of local laws`

DECLARE `S52 Revocation Grounds` HAS
    `relates to a matter affecting dogs or the keeping of dogs`                                                              IS A BOOLEAN
    `in the Governor's opinion, the local law (or the manner of its administration) is unduly oppressive`                    IS A BOOLEAN
    `in the Governor's opinion, the local law (or the manner of its administration) is repugnant to the provisions of this Act` IS A BOOLEAN
    `in the Governor's opinion, the local law (or the manner of its administration) is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act` IS A BOOLEAN

@ref Dog Act 1976 (WA) s. 52(1)

-- or inconsistent with the provisions of this Act" (s 52(1)) states no test
-- of its own. Delegated to the Governor's own opinion, per s 52(1)'s own
-- "in the opinion of the Governor" language -- the same treatment this
-- corpus already gives F-REPEATEDLY-TENDENCY and F-33H-SATISFACTION-STANDARD
-- in dog-act-1976.l4. The two possible subjects of that opinion -- "that
-- local law" itself, or "the manner in which that local law is
-- administered" -- are folded into one generic ground-check field per
-- limb below, since the grounds test is identical either way.
GIVEN g IS A `S52 Revocation Grounds`
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`the Governor may revoke a local law (or part of it) under s 52(1)` g MEANS
        g's `relates to a matter affecting dogs or the keeping of dogs`
    AND (   g's `in the Governor's opinion, the local law (or the manner of its administration) is unduly oppressive`

         OR g's `in the Governor's opinion, the local law (or the manner of its administration) is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act`)
